texts.text: Ladies and gentlemen, good morning and welcome to Almaty Airport. The check-in desks are on the first floor, on your left. Flight 427 to Astana is now open for check-in. The flight leaves at 10:45 from Gate 12. Please keep your bag with you at all times. Do not leave your bag alone. Please have your passport and ticket ready. Have a good flight, and thank you for flying with Sky Steppe Airlines.

Ladies and gentlemen, welcome on board Steppe Air Flight 427 from Almaty to Astana. My name is Dana, and I am your cabin manager today. Please put your bags under the seat in front of you. Fasten your seat belt and turn off your phone. The exits are at the front and at the back. After take off, we serve tea, coffee and a hot meal. We land in Astana at 10:45. Sit back and enjoy the flight. Thank you!

Attention, please! The train to Astana leaves from platform 3 at 10:45. Please go to platform 3 now. The train to Shymkent is late. It now leaves at 11:20 from platform 5. We are very sorry. Please stand behind the yellow line. The train is coming. When you get on the train, mind the gap. Do not leave your bags alone. Have a good trip, and thank you for travelling with us.

Welcome to the Almaty metro. The next station is Abay. Please stand back from the doors. The doors are closing. This is Abay. Please take your bags and mind the gap. Give your seat to old people and to mothers with small children. Please take off your backpack in the train. Do not eat or drink here, and speak quietly on the phone. The next station is Baikonur. Thank you, and have a nice day.

Hello, passengers! This bus goes to the city centre. Next stop: Abay Street. Please hold on, the bus is moving. Please give your seat to old people and to mothers with small children. Do not stand near the doors. Next stop: Green Market. The doors are opening. Please mind the step. The next stop is Central Park. Please take all your bags with you. Thank you for travelling with us. Have a nice day!

Hello! Where are you going? The Green Bazaar? No problem. Please fasten your seat belt. I'm Nurlan, and I love this city. Look, there are the mountains! They are beautiful in the morning. The traffic is very bad today, so I can take a small street. It's faster. Do you like Almaty? Many people come here for the apples and the mountains. OK, here we are. That's two thousand tenge. Have a nice day!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. This is your captain speaking. Welcome on board the ferry Caspian Star. We are leaving Aktau now. The sea is calm today, and the weather is good. The cafe is on the second deck. It has hot food and tea. Please do not run on the deck. Children must stay with their parents. Look to the left. There are seals in the water! We arrive at 9:00 tomorrow morning. Enjoy the trip!

Good afternoon, and welcome to the Hotel Altyn Tau. Can I have your passport, please? Thank you, Mr Arman. Your room is 215, on the second floor. Here is your key card. Breakfast is from 7:00 to 10:00 in the restaurant. There is a gym and a small pool on the first floor. The internet is free, and the password is on your card. The lift is on your right. Do you need help with your bags? Enjoy your stay!

Hello, everyone, and welcome to Charyn Canyon! My name is Aigerim, and I am your guide today. Look around you. The rocks are red, orange and yellow. People call it the Valley of Castles. Please stay on the path, and don't go near the edge. It is hot here, so drink a lot of water. We walk for two hours, and then we have lunch by the river. Let's go!

Good morning, and welcome to the Astana city bus tour! I'm Timur, your guide today. On your left is the Baiterek tower. It looks like a tree with a golden egg. On your right is a big park. People walk and ride bikes there in summer. Astana is a young city with many new buildings. Our next stop is in five minutes. Please don't stand up on the bus. Thank you!

Attention, shoppers! Welcome to Fresh Day supermarket. Today, our fruit and vegetables are very cheap. Apples, bananas and oranges are half price. Tomatoes and potatoes are cheap too. Come to the fruit and vegetable section on your right. Our bread is fresh every morning. It is warm and very good. Please take a basket at the door. The shop closes at 22:00 today. Thank you for shopping with us, and have a nice evening!

Good afternoon, shoppers, and welcome to Sunny Mall! The food court is on the third floor, and the cinema is on the fourth floor. Today at 4:00 there is a free dance show for children. Attention, please! We have a little boy here. His name is Ali, and he is five. Ali's parents, please come to the information desk on the ground floor. The mall closes at 22:00. Thank you for shopping with us!

Hello and welcome to the Sunny Table! Please sit down. My name is Arman and I am your waiter today. Here is our menu. We have soup, chicken with rice, and a big green salad. For dessert, there is chocolate cake or ice cream. To drink, we have tea, coffee, orange juice and water. The tea is very good here. Are you ready to order? No problem, take your time. I can come back in five minutes.

Good morning, and welcome to the City Family Clinic. Please take a number from the machine near the door. When you see your number on the screen, go to the window. Do you have an appointment? Please come ten minutes early. Doctor Madina is in room 104 today, and Doctor Bekov is in room 112. Please wear a mask in the waiting room and turn off the sound on your phone. Children, please don't run. Thank you for waiting.

Hello, everyone, and welcome to the city library! I'm Saule, the librarian. On this floor there are books for children. Upstairs you can find books in English, Kazakh and Russian. You can take three books for two weeks. Please bring them back on time. Speak quietly, please, and don't eat near the books. You can use the computers for one hour. Every Saturday at 11:00 we have a reading club for children. See you there!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the City History Museum. Please follow me. In this room you can see old Kazakh clothes. Look at this dress. It is red and gold, and it is very beautiful. And here is a yurt. Families lived in yurts in the steppe. You can go inside, but please take off your shoes. Don't touch the glass, and please don't take photos with a flash. Our next room is upstairs. This way, please!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Star Cinema in Astana! Tonight is a very special night. It is the first show of the new film, The Snow Leopard. The director and the actors are here with us! Please give them a big hand. The film is two hours long. Please turn off your phones, and don't talk during the film. Popcorn and drinks are at the back. Now sit back, relax and enjoy the show!

Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the Almaty Concert Hall! Tonight we have a wonderful programme. First, the city youth orchestra plays music by Kazakh composers. Then, after a short break, Aruzhan sings songs from the steppe. The concert is about two hours long. Please turn off your phones now. You can't take photos or videos during the music. The break is twenty minutes, and there is tea and coffee in the cafe. Thank you, and enjoy the evening!

Hello, hello! Come here, my friend! Look at these apples. They're from Almaty, big and sweet! Try one, please. It's free! I also have dried apricots, raisins and walnuts. My dried apricots are very good with tea. Do you like bread? This bread is still hot. It's from the oven this morning. Apples are five hundred tenge a kilo. For you, today, only four hundred! Come back tomorrow. Thank you, and have a good day!

Hello, children! Welcome to the zoo. My name is Aigerim and I am your guide today. Look, here are the monkeys! They eat bananas and other fruit. Over there, you can see a big brown bear. Bears eat fish, berries and honey. Now look at the giraffe. It is very tall! It eats leaves from the trees. Please remember one thing. Do not feed the animals. Our food is bad for them. Now, let's go and see the lions!

Good evening. Here is the news. In Astana, a new park opens today. It has a big lake, a playground and a bike path. In Shymkent, there is a food festival this weekend. People can try plov, bread and fresh fruit. In Aktau, a family finds a small seal on the beach. Now the seal is safe at the sea centre. And in sport, the Almaty girls' volleyball team wins the cup. That's the news. Good night.

Good morning, and here is the weather for today. In Almaty it is sunny and warm, about twenty degrees. Take your sunglasses! In Astana it is cold and windy, only five degrees. Wear a warm jacket and a hat. In Shymkent it is hot and sunny all day. In Aktau it is cloudy, and there is rain in the afternoon, so take an umbrella. Tomorrow is sunny everywhere. Have a lovely day!

Are you hungry? Do you love pizza? Then come to Tasty Steppe Cafe in Shymkent! We have big pizzas, hot soup and fresh salads. Our food is fast, cheap and very good. Every Friday, children eat for free! We are open every day from 9:00 to 23:00. We are on Baitursynov Street, near the park. Call us now, or come and see us today! Tasty Steppe Cafe: good food for the whole family!

Hi, everyone, and welcome to Easy Travel, the podcast for new travellers! I'm Madina, your host. Today's episode is about Burabay. Burabay is a beautiful place in the north of Kazakhstan. There are blue lakes, green forests and big rocks. You can swim, walk and ride a bike there. In this episode, my friend Arman tells us about his trip. He loves the lakes, but he doesn't like the mosquitoes! So listen and enjoy. Let's start!

And here we go, the final of the city cup in Shymkent! The red team plays the blue team today. The stadium is full and very loud. Number nine, Arman, has the ball. He runs past one player, then two. Can he score? He shoots! Oh, the goalkeeper catches it. What a save! Now the blue team attacks. Timur passes to Ali. Ali shoots, and it's a goal! The fans sing and jump. What a great game!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the city stadium in Astana! Tonight the Astana Stars play the Almaty Eagles. Please find your seat now. The match starts at 19:00. Please don't stand on the seats. Don't throw bottles or food. The exits are on the left and on the right. Are you ready? Let's hear it for the Eagles! And now, let's hear it for the Stars! Thank you. Have a great evening and enjoy the game!

This is the Kazakh steppe. It is very big. In summer, the grass is green and yellow, and the sun is hot. Here we can see a family of saigas. Saigas are small brown animals with big noses. Their noses help them in the dust and in the cold air. They eat grass and drink from small lakes. In winter, the steppe is white and very cold. But the saiga can live here. It is a strong animal.

Hello and welcome to My Breakfast! Today I can show you my favourite breakfast. It is very easy. First, take two eggs. Break the eggs into a hot pan. Add a little salt. Cook them for three minutes. Now, take some bread. Put it in the toaster. Next, boil the water and make a cup of tea. Put the eggs on a plate with the bread. Add some butter. And there you are! Breakfast is ready. Enjoy it!

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming. My name is Dana Seitova, and I work for the city of Aktau. Today we have good news. There is a new park by the Caspian Sea. It has trees, a playground and a long path for bikes. It opens on Saturday at 10:00. Everyone can come, and it is free. Now, a question from the radio, please. Is there a cafe? Yes, there is a small cafe. Thank you.

This is an important weather warning for Almaty and the mountains. There is a big storm tonight. There is strong wind, heavy rain and snow in the mountains. Please stay at home after 18:00. Close your windows and doors. Don't park your car under trees. Don't go to the mountains tomorrow. Children, please stay inside. Charge your phone now. Listen to the radio for news. We give new information every hour. Stay safe, and thank you for listening.

Good morning, students, and welcome to a new school day! This is your head teacher speaking. Here is today's timetable. The first lesson starts at 8:30. At 10:15, there is a short break. Lunch is at 12:30 in the dining room. The library is open all day. You can read books and do your homework there. After lessons, there is sport in the gym. Bring your trainers, please! Listen to your teachers. Have a good day!

Good morning, class! How are you today? Please sit down and open your books. Today our topic is food. First, we learn ten new words. Then you work in pairs. Ask your partner: What do you like for breakfast? Write the answers in your notebook. At the end, tell the class about your partner. Don't worry about mistakes. Mistakes are good. They help you learn. Are you ready? Great, let's start!

Good afternoon. Thank you for this interview. My name is Aigerim Nurlanova. I am from Karaganda, but I live in Astana now. I am a waiter in a small hotel. I speak Kazakh, Russian and English. I can use a computer well. I am friendly and I am never late. I want to work at your hotel because it is big and modern. I can start next month. Do you have any questions for me? Thank you.

Good morning, Madina, and welcome to the team! I'm Nurlan, your manager. This is our office. Your desk is here, next to the window. This is Asel. She can help you this week. The kitchen is on the left, and the meeting room is on the right. We have a team meeting every Monday at 9:30. Your first task is easy. Please read these documents and answer our emails. Lunch is at one o'clock. Welcome again!

Hello, everyone. Thank you for coming. My name is Timur, and this is our project, Green School. We want clean and green schools in Shymkent. This year there are new trees at five schools. Students also collect paper and bottles. Look at this picture. Now there is less rubbish in the schoolyards. Teachers are happy, and students are happy too. What is next? Next year we want ten more schools. We need your help. Thank you for listening!

Hi Aruzhan, it's Dana. Are you busy? Please call me back. I have a question about Saturday. Do you want to go to Kolsay Lakes with me? My brother has a car, and there are two free seats. We can leave at 7:00 in the morning. The lakes are beautiful in autumn. Bring warm clothes, good shoes and some food. I can bring tea and bread. Please call me or send me a message tonight. Okay, bye! Talk soon!

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Young Ideas Conference in Almaty! We are very happy to see you here. Today there are ten speakers from all over Kazakhstan. They are young, and they have big ideas. Listen, ask questions and meet new people. Lunch is at 13:00 in the main hall. Please turn off your phones now. Remember, every big project starts with a small idea. Maybe your idea is next! Now let's start. Enjoy the day!

Good evening, teachers, parents and friends. My name is Ali. Today is a very special day for us. We are happy, and we are a little sad. Our school is like a second home. Thank you, teachers, for your help every day. Thank you, mum and dad, for your love. Friends, remember our trips, our games and our jokes. Now we start a new life. Be brave, be kind and work hard. Congratulations, everyone!

Good afternoon, judges and friends. Our topic today is this: students must wear school uniforms. Our team says yes. Here are our reasons. First, uniforms are simple. Students don't think about clothes every morning. Second, uniforms are fair. Rich students and poor students look the same. Third, a uniform makes a team. We are one school. Maybe uniforms are boring, but they help students learn. Please vote for our team. Thank you.

Good morning, Your Honour. My name is Arman Bekov. I live in flat 25 on Abai Street in Astana. My neighbour lives above me. Every night, he plays very loud music. It starts at 23:00 and stops at 3:00. I can't sleep. My children can't sleep. I ask him to stop, but he says no. Our building has rules. There is no loud noise after 22:00. Please help us. We want a quiet home. Thank you.

Hello everyone! My name is Ali and I am twelve years old. I live in Almaty with my mum, my dad and my little sister. I go to school every day. My favourite subject is English because it is fun and easy. After school I play football with my friends in the park. On Saturday I visit my grandmother. She makes very good tea and cakes. I like reading books, watching cartoons and listening to music. Nice to meet you!

Hello, everyone! Thank you for coming to my birthday party! Today I am ten years old, and I am very happy. Please come in and take a hat. First, we can play some games. There are balloons in the garden. Then we can dance to music. After that, there is a big chocolate cake! My mum makes it every year. And look, there are lots of presents on the table. Thank you, my friends! Let's have fun!

Dear Grandma, hello from Aktau! We are on holiday by the Caspian Sea. The weather is great. It is hot and sunny every day. The sea is blue and warm. Every morning, we swim and play on the beach. My dad sleeps under a big umbrella. My sister makes sand castles. In the evening, we eat fish and ice cream. Our hotel is small but very nice. I miss you. See you soon! Love, Madina.

Okay, everyone, come and sit by the fire! What a great day! We swim in the river, we play football and we cook fish. Well done, team! Now, tomorrow. We get up at 7:00. Breakfast is at 7:30. Then we go to the forest. Please bring water and a hat. Here are the rules. Don't walk alone at night. Don't go too near the fire. Stay with your group. Now, let's sing a song and then sleep. Good night, everyone!

Hi! My name is Timur and I am eight years old. On Sunday, I go to the park with my family. My mum, my dad and my little sister come too. The park is big and green. My dad and I play football. My sister likes the swings. My mum reads a book under a tree. At one o'clock, we have a picnic. We eat sandwiches and apples. Then we feed the ducks. I love Sundays in the park!

Hello from my home in Almaty! Today is a rainy day. It is cold and grey outside. There is water in the street, and I can't go out. But that's OK. I am at home with my cat. I drink hot tea and I read a good book. My brother plays computer games. My mother cooks soup in the kitchen. It smells very nice. In the evening, we watch a film together. I like rainy days at home!

Hello, everybody! Are you ready? Let's go! Stand up and smile. First, we walk on the spot. One, two, three, four. Good! Now arms up, and arms down. Again! Now we jump. Jump, jump, jump! Come on, you can do it! Now ten squats. Down and up, down and up. Great work! Drink some water. Breathe in and breathe out. Last one: run on the spot. Faster, faster! And stop. Well done, everyone. See you tomorrow!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Charyn Canyon! My name is Nurlan, and I am your guide today. Please listen carefully. Our walk is three hours. It is very hot here, so drink a lot of water. Wear your hat and sunglasses. Stay on the path and stay with the group. Don't go near the edge. Don't feed the animals. Are you tired? Please tell me. We can stop and rest. Are you ready? Okay, let's go!

This is mission control at Baikonur. Good morning, everyone. Today is a big day. Our rocket is ready, and the sky is clear. There are three astronauts on board. They are calm and happy. The engines are on. Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. Lift off! The rocket goes up into the sky. It is very fast. Everything is okay. In six hours, our crew is at the space station. Good luck, crew!

Hello, friends! Let's play with words. Read fast, but read clearly. Ready? Six silly sheep sleep on the steppe. Again! Six silly sheep sleep on the steppe. Now this one: big black bugs eat big brown buns. Good! Now a rhyme. A cat in a hat sits on a mat. The cat is fat, and that is that! Last one: Dana drinks a drop of dark tea daily. Faster, faster! Well done, you are a tongue twister star!

Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Almaty International Airport. Check-in for Steppe Air Flight 427 to Aktau is now open in Hall B. Remember that liquids in your hand luggage have to be in small bottles. The flight is going to leave from Gate 12 at 10:45. Boarding will start forty minutes before departure. Passengers with small children should come to the gate first. This is the final call for passenger Timur Seitkali, travelling to Astana on Flight 215. Please go to Gate 7 immediately, the doors will close in five minutes. Thank you, and have a pleasant flight.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome on board Sky Steppe Flight 318 from Astana to Shymkent. My name is Aigerim, and I am your senior cabin attendant today. Please put your bags in the lockers above you or under the seat in front of you. Fasten your seat belt and keep it fastened while you are sitting. In about twenty minutes we will serve hot drinks and a light meal. Our flight time today is shorter than usual, only one hour and fifty minutes. We will land in Shymkent at 14:20. Enjoy the flight, and thank you.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. This is an announcement for passengers travelling to Astana. The train to Astana is now arriving at platform 3. It will leave at 14:30. First class passengers should go to carriages one and two, at the front of the train. All other passengers can use carriages three to eight. You have to keep your bags with you at all times. When you get on the train, please mind the gap between the train and the platform. The journey will take about twelve hours. Thank you for travelling with us, and have a good journey!

Welcome to the Almaty metro. This train is going to Moskva station. The next station is Abay. Please stand clear of the doors, the doors are closing. Hold the handrail and do not lean on the doors. Passengers should give their seats to older people and passengers with small children. Please take off your backpack in a busy carriage. Do not eat or drink on the train. If you see a bag without an owner, you have to tell the station staff. Next station, Baikonur. Change here for the airport bus. Doors open on the right. Thank you for travelling with us.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome on the Green Line bus to Astana city centre. Please pay with your travel card when you get on. If you haven't got a card, you can buy a ticket from the driver, but it's more expensive. Next stop, Central Park. Older passengers should sit in the front seats, near the driver. Please don't put your bags on the seats. Next stop, the Main Library. Passengers for the university should get off here and walk for five minutes. Mind the step when you leave the bus. Thank you for travelling with us, and have a lovely day.

So, you're going to Kok Tobe hill, yes? Good choice! Sit back and relax. Is this your first time in Almaty? Wow, you're going to love it. Today the traffic is worse than yesterday, because it's Friday. Everyone wants to go to the mountains after work. So I'm going to take a different road, along the river. It's longer, but it's faster. Look on the left, that's the Green Bazaar. You should buy some dried apricots there tomorrow. And Almaty apples are the best in the country, my grandmother always said that. Here we are. That's two thousand tenge, please. Enjoy the view, my friend!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. Welcome on board the ferry Caspian Star from Aktau to Baku. We left the port twenty minutes ago, and the sea is calm tonight. Our journey will take about eighteen hours, so we are going to arrive tomorrow afternoon. Dinner is served in the restaurant on the second deck until 21:30. Children have to stay with an adult on the open deck. The wind is stronger at night, so you should wear a warm jacket outside. If you are lucky, you will see seals near the ship tomorrow morning. Sleep well!

Good afternoon, and welcome to the Hotel Altyn Tau. Here is your key card. You're in room 512 on the fifth floor. It has a lovely view of the mountains. The lift is just behind you, on the right. Breakfast is from 7:00 to 10:30 in the restaurant on the ground floor. You should try our baursaks, they're the best in town. The swimming pool and the gym are open all day, and they're free for guests. The internet password is on the back of your card. If you need anything, just call reception. Have a wonderful stay, Mr Nurlanov!

Okay, everyone, can you all hear me? Welcome to Charyn Canyon! Some people call it the little brother of the Grand Canyon in America. It isn't as big, but many visitors say it's more beautiful. These red rocks are millions of years old. The wind and the river made these strange shapes. This part is called the Valley of Castles. Can you see why? Now we are going to walk down to the river. It takes about forty minutes. The path is narrow, so you should wear good shoes and take some water. At the river we'll have lunch. Ready? Let's go!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome aboard our city tour of Almaty! On your left, you can see the Opera and Ballet Theatre. It's one of the most beautiful buildings in the city. Now look to the right. That building is newer and much taller than the buildings around it. We're now driving past Panfilov Park. It's greener and quieter than the busy streets, and people love walking there. And now look up! Those are the mountains. In winter, they're even more beautiful, with white snow on top. Our next stop is in ten minutes. Thank you!

Good afternoon, shoppers, and welcome to Dala Mall. Here is some great news for you. Today only, all winter jackets are thirty per cent cheaper on the second floor. Our biggest sale of the year starts this weekend, so don't miss it! In the food court, every coffee comes with a free cake until 15:00. Families should visit the toy shop on the ground floor, where children's books are half price. Please remember that the mall closes earlier on Sunday, at 20:00. Thank you for shopping with us, and have a great day!

Good morning, shoppers, and welcome to Sunrise Shopping Centre! This weekend we are having our biggest sale of the year. Some things are half price! On the ground floor, you can find shoes, bags and beautiful jewellery. Go up to the first floor for clothes for men, women and children. The second floor has phones, computers and toys. Hungry? Our food court is on the top floor, and it has the best views in the city. You can try Kazakh, Italian and Korean food there. Please remember that the centre closes at 22:00. Thank you, and happy shopping!

Hello and welcome to Shanyrak! Sit anywhere you like. The table by the window is the sunniest. My name is Madina, and my mother and I opened this place three years ago. Here is the menu. Our most popular dish is beshbarmak, and today we have fresh lagman too. If you'd like something lighter, you should try the vegetable soup. For dessert, I recommend the honey cake. It's my grandmother's recipe, and it's sweeter than any cake in Shymkent! Would you like some tea while you decide? We have black tea with milk, the Kazakh way. Take your time. I'll be back in a minute.

Good morning, and welcome to the City Family Clinic. Please take a ticket from the machine by the door and wait for your number on the screen. If you have an appointment, go straight to reception with your ID card. Patients without an appointment will have to wait a little longer today. The morning is our busiest time, and the afternoon is usually quieter. Please turn your phone to silent in the waiting room. Children should stay with their parents at all times. Doctor Sarsenova is running twenty minutes late. Next patient, Mr Arman Bekov, please go to room 3. Thank you.

Attention, please. This is an announcement for all library visitors. This week we got more than fifty new books. You can find them on the big table near the front door. Please remember that the second floor is a quiet zone. You mustn't talk or use your phone there. If you want to study with friends, you should use the group rooms on the first floor. You can borrow five books at a time for two weeks. Please bring them back on time! The library closes in fifteen minutes. Thank you, and see you tomorrow!

Hello, everyone, and welcome to the History Museum in Astana. My name is Dana, and I'm going to be your guide today. Here you can see some very old jewellery. Women in Kazakhstan wore these silver rings and bracelets hundreds of years ago. Now look at this yurt. Families lived in yurts like this one and moved them from place to place. And this is the most famous thing in our museum: a golden warrior costume. It has thousands of small gold pieces on it. Please don't touch anything, because everything here is very old. Now, let's go upstairs!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Star Cinema! Tonight's film will start in five minutes, so please find your seats now. Before the film begins, please switch off your mobile phones. Also, please don't talk during the film. If you have to leave, please go quietly. Did you forget to buy snacks? Don't worry! You can still get popcorn and cold drinks at the counter near the door. The emergency exits are on the left and on the right. Sit back, relax and enjoy the film!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Grand Steppe Theatre! Tonight is a very special night. Our young orchestra is going to play music from all over Kazakhstan. In the first part, you will hear the dombra and the kobyz, two of our oldest instruments. After that, there will be a break of twenty minutes. Drinks and snacks are in the hall on the first floor. In the second part, our best singer, Aruzhan Tulegenova, will join the orchestra. Before we start, please turn off your phones. Photos and videos are not allowed during the show. Thank you, and enjoy the evening!

Come here, come here, my dear! Welcome to the Green Bazaar! Look at these apples. They're the sweetest apples in Almaty, I promise. Try one, it's free! These dried apricots came from Shymkent yesterday. They're softer and cheaper than in the supermarket. And these raisins? Perfect for plov. My wife baked this bread this morning, so it's still warm. Smell it! One round loaf costs two hundred tenge. If you buy a kilo of apricots, I'll give you the bread for free. No? Then half a kilo? Okay, okay, I'll give you a better price. You're my favourite customer today!

Hello, everyone, and welcome to the big cat house at the Almaty Zoo! My name is Dana, and I'm a keeper here. This beautiful animal is our snow leopard, Barys. He came to us five years ago. Snow leopards live high in the mountains, so he loves cold weather. Look at his long, thick tail. It helps him to keep his balance on the rocks. He usually sleeps in the afternoon, but he's very active in the morning. Please don't knock on the glass, and you must never feed the animals. Next, we're going to visit the camels. Follow me!

Good evening, and here is the news. In Shymkent, a new park opened today. It is the biggest park in the south of the country, with a lake and a long cycling path. In Astana, the weather was colder than usual this week. Tomorrow will be sunny, but people should still wear warm coats. A young student from Pavlodar won first prize in an international chess competition. Her name is Aigerim, and she is only twelve years old. And finally, a lost dog travelled two hundred kilometres to find its family in Kostanay. That's all for now. Thank you for watching, and good night.

Good evening and here is the weather for tomorrow. In the morning it will be cold and cloudy in Astana, with a temperature of minus five degrees. In the afternoon the sun will come out, but the wind will be strong, so please wear a warm hat and gloves. In Almaty it will be warmer, about eight degrees, and there may be some light rain in the evening. On Sunday the weather will be sunny and dry everywhere. Have a nice weekend!

Are you bored at the weekend? Do you want to try something new? Then come to the Steppe Fun Festival in Burabay! This Saturday and Sunday there will be live music, horse shows and the tastiest food in the region. Children can ride ponies, make kites and play games by the lake. It's bigger and better than last year! Tickets are cheaper online, so don't wait. Buy yours now on our website, or call us today. Bring your family, bring your friends, and bring your camera! The Steppe Fun Festival in Burabay. You're going to have the best weekend ever!

Hello and welcome to Healthy Days, the podcast about small habits with big results. I'm your host, Nurlan, and I'm recording this episode in my kitchen in Astana. Last month I decided to change three things in my life. First, I stopped looking at my phone before bed. Second, I started walking to work every day. Third, I drank more water and less coffee. Was it easy? No, not at all! But now I sleep better and I feel happier. Today my guest, a young teacher from Almaty, is going to share her favourite habits. So get a cup of tea, and let's begin!

And here we go, the final minutes of the big match between the Almaty Eagles and the Astana Wolves! The score is one all, and the fans are on their feet! Timur Akhmetov has the ball on the left. He's faster than the defender, and he's running towards the goal. What a pass to Ali in the middle! Ali shoots, and the goalkeeper saves it! Now the Wolves have to attack. Only two minutes left. Corner kick for the Eagles. Ali jumps higher than everyone, he heads the ball, and it's in the net! Goal! The Almaty Eagles are the champions!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our school sports day! We have four teams today: Red, Blue, Green and Yellow. The first race was the hundred metres, and Timur from the Red Team was the fastest. He ran faster than last year! In the long race, Aigerim from the Green Team came first. So, here are the results so far: the Red Team is in first place, but the Green Team is very close. The next race is the relay, and it's going to start in ten minutes. Everybody, cheer for your team as loudly as you can!

Here, in the wide steppe of central Kazakhstan, spring arrives late. For months, the land was white and silent. Now the snow is melting, and the first green grass is coming up. This is the saiga antelope. It has a strange, large nose. This nose helps it to breathe cold winter air and hot, dusty summer air. Every spring, thousands of saigas walk hundreds of kilometres to find fresh grass. The young ones are born in May. After only a few days, they can run faster than a person. Life on the steppe is hard, but the saiga is a true survivor.

Hello, and welcome back to Cooking at Home! Today we're going to make baursak, my favourite Kazakh bread. It's easy, I promise! First, you have to mix warm milk, a little sugar and some yeast in a bowl. Then add flour and a pinch of salt. Now you should cover the bowl and wait for one hour. Next, cut it into small squares. Heat some oil in a big pan. Be careful, because hot oil is dangerous! Fry the baursak until they're golden. You should eat them warm with a cup of tea. Delicious! See you next week!

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for coming. My name is Dana Seitova, and I speak for the city of Shymkent. Today I have some good news. Next spring, the city is going to open a new park by the river. It will be bigger than the old central park, and it will have a skating rink, a small library and long bike paths. First, we have to repair two old bridges, so some roads will close in March. Now I can take one question. Yes, please? Will the park be free? Yes, it will be free for everyone. Thank you all very much.

This is an emergency weather warning for Almaty and the Almaty region. A strong storm is coming from the mountains tonight. Forecasters say the wind will be stronger than last week, and there will be heavy snow after midnight. Please stay at home if you can. You should not drive on mountain roads, and you have to keep children and pets inside. Charge your phone now and keep a torch near your bed. Do not park your car under old trees. Schools in the region will close tomorrow morning. We will give you the next update at 21:00. Stay safe and look after your neighbours.

Good morning, students, this is your morning announcement. Please listen carefully. Today the timetable is a little different. Classes will finish at 13:30 because the teachers have a meeting this afternoon. Grade nine students have to bring their sports kit, because the volleyball final is after lunch. Last year we came second, so this year let's win! On Friday, the school is going to hold a book fair in the main hall. Bring your old books and swap them with friends. Also, the canteen has a new menu, and it is healthier than before. Finally, please don't run in the corridors. Have a wonderful day!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to today's lesson. Please sit down and open your notebooks. Last week we talked about travel, and you did a great job. Today we are going to learn how to compare cities. First, we will read a short text about Astana and Almaty. Which city is bigger? Which one is colder in winter? Then you will work in pairs and write five sentences. You should use words like better, older and the most beautiful. At the end, every pair has to read one sentence aloud. Don't worry about mistakes, because mistakes help us learn. Are you ready? Great, let's begin!

Thank you for inviting me today. My name is Arman Kassymov, and I am from Karaganda. Two years ago I finished college, and then I worked at a small travel agency in Astana. I helped customers plan their holidays, answered phone calls and wrote emails in English and Russian. It was busy, but I learned a lot. I am friendly, I am good with people, and I always finish my work on time. Now I want a bigger challenge, and your hotel is one of the best in the city. In the future, I am going to study tourism management. Thank you for your time.

Welcome to the team, Aigerim! We're happy to have you here. Let me show you around the office. This is our open space, and your desk is next to the window. That's Nurlan, our designer, and over there is Madina. She looks after our social media. They will help you this week. Your first task is easy. You have to check our new product descriptions and correct any mistakes. Every Monday at 10:00 we have a team meeting The kitchen is at the end of the corridor, and the coffee there is better than in the cafe downstairs! Great, let's get started.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for coming to our presentation. Six months ago, our team started a project: online English lessons for villages near Taraz. Today I want to show you the results. In the first month, we had only twenty students. Now we have more than two hundred! Our lessons are cheaper than lessons in the city, and parents say they are more convenient. But we also had problems. The internet was slow in some places, so we recorded our lessons. What are our next steps? Next year, we are going to open lessons in three more regions. Thank you for listening.

Hi Madina, it's Aruzhan! Sorry, I know you're busy, but this is important. So, Saturday! Nurlan and I are going to go to the mountains. We're going to take the bus at 9:30 from the city centre. Do you want to come with us? It'll be fun, I promise! Bring warm clothes, because it's colder up there. Oh, and guess what happened yesterday? I lost my phone in a cafe! I looked everywhere, and I was really worried. Then a kind waiter found it under a table. I was so happy! Anyway, I have to go now. Please call me back tonight, okay? Bye!

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Young Ideas Conference here in Astana! It is a great pleasure to see so many people in this hall. This year we have more speakers than ever before, from Almaty, Aktobe and Kyzylorda. Ten years ago, this conference was very small. We met in a tiny classroom with only thirty guests. Today it is the biggest youth event in the region. Over the next two days, you will hear about science, art, business and the environment. Ask questions and share your ideas. Remember, every big change starts with one small idea. Let's begin!

Dear teachers, parents and classmates, good evening! Today is one of the most important days of our lives. Eleven years ago, we came to this school as little children with big backpacks. We were shy. Now look at us! We are taller, smarter and maybe a little more confident. Our teachers helped us every day, even when we didn't want to do our homework. Thank you for your patience. Tomorrow we are going to start a new chapter. Some of us will study in Almaty, and some will travel abroad. But we will never forget this place. Congratulations, everyone, we did it!

Good afternoon, judges and students. Today's topic is: should students wear school uniforms? Our team believes that the answer is yes. First, uniforms make life easier. In the morning, you don't have to think about clothes, so you have more time for breakfast. Second, uniforms are cheaper than fashionable clothes, and that helps families. Third, when everyone looks the same, students worry less about clothes and more about learning. Some people say uniforms are boring. Maybe, but schools can let students choose the colours. For these reasons, we think uniforms help schools. Thank you, and we are happy to answer your questions.

Your Honour, thank you for hearing this case today. My client, Mr Bolat Ospanov, lives in a flat on Abay Street in Almaty. Last year, a new neighbour moved into the flat above him. After that, the neighbour played loud music almost every night until 2:00. My client wrote three polite letters, but nothing changed. He also asked the building manager for help. Because of the noise, he couldn't sleep, and he was often late for work. The building rules say that residents have to be quiet after 23:00. We ask the court to tell the neighbour to follow these rules. Thank you.

Hi! Let me tell you a little about myself. My name is Aruzhan, and I'm sixteen years old. I live in Pavlodar with my parents, my grandmother and my younger brother, Ali. Our flat is small but very warm and cosy. My mum is a nurse, and my dad works at a factory. In my free time, I love drawing and playing the dombra. Last summer, I went to a music camp near Burabay, and it was the best summer of my life. Next year, I'm going to finish school. Then I want to study design in Astana. Nice to meet you!

Good evening, dear friends and family! Can I have your attention, please? Thank you all for coming tonight to celebrate my grandmother's seventieth birthday. Apa, you are the kindest and wisest person in our family. When I was little, you baked the best baursaks in the whole of Shymkent, and you told me wonderful stories every night. You taught me to be patient and to help other people. Today, you look younger and happier than ever! We hope you will stay healthy and strong for many more years. So please, everyone, raise your glasses. To our dear Apa! Happy birthday!

Hello, everyone. Today I'm going to tell you about my summer holiday. Last July, my family and I went to Aktau, on the Caspian Sea. We went by plane. The weather was very hot, so we went to the beach every day. My little brother Arman built a big sandcastle, and I learned to swim better. One evening, we ate fresh fish in a small restaurant near the sea. It was the best fish of my life! On the last day, I didn't want to go home. It was my favourite holiday ever. Thank you for listening!

Okay, everyone, come and sit around the fire! What a great day we had today! In the morning, we walked to the lake, and some of you swam in the cold water. After lunch, the Blue Team won the football match. Well done! Tomorrow is going to be even more exciting. We're going to climb the hill near the camp, so you should wear good shoes. We'll have breakfast at 8:00, and we'll leave at 9:00. Now, some rules. You have to stay with your group. Don't go into the forest alone at night. Now, who wants to sing a song?

It's a beautiful Sunday morning, and I'm walking through the park near my house in Kostanay. The air is fresh and cool. Autumn is my favourite season, because the trees turn yellow, orange and red. Look, there's an old man feeding the pigeons, and two little girls are collecting leaves. A young couple is jogging with their dog. Last spring, the city planted new flowers along this path, and now it's more colourful than before. I usually come here after work, but mornings are quieter. Tomorrow I'm going to bring my camera and take some photos. What a lovely, peaceful walk!

Dear diary, it's Saturday, and it's raining again in Almaty. I wanted to go to the mountains with my friends, but we had to cancel our trip. At first I was sad, but now I'm actually quite happy. I made a big cup of tea with milk and found a warm blanket. My cat, Barsik, is sleeping next to me on the sofa. I'm reading an old adventure novel, and it's better than any film. Outside, people are running with umbrellas, and the streets are shining. Later, I'm going to cook soup for dinner. Sometimes a quiet rainy day is the best kind of day.

Good morning, everybody! Are you ready to move? Let's go! First, we're going to warm up. March on the spot and swing your arms, nice and easy. Great! Now, ten squats. Keep your back straight and go down slowly. One, two, three, you're doing brilliantly! Remember, you should breathe in and breathe out. Don't hold your breath! Next, jumping jacks for thirty seconds. Faster, faster! You're stronger than you think! Last week, this was difficult for you, and today it's easier. Okay, time for a short break. Drink some water. Then we'll do our final exercise. Come on, team, finish strong!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Kolsay Lakes! My name is Timur, and I'm your guide today. Before we start, please listen carefully. Our hike is about eight kilometres, and it will take five hours. The path to the second lake is steeper than it looks, so walk slowly. You have to stay with the group at all times. Please don't leave the path, and don't feed the animals. You should drink water often, even if you don't feel thirsty. The weather in the mountains changes quickly, so keep your jacket in your bag. If you feel tired, tell me. Right, let's go!

This is Baikonur mission control. All systems are ready. The rocket is standing on the launch pad, and three astronauts are on board. The weather is clear and the wind is calm, so we are going to launch on time. The crew will fly to the International Space Station. Their journey will take about six hours. They are going to stay there for six months and do many science experiments. Ten seconds to launch. Nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one. Ignition! And liftoff! The rocket is climbing higher and higher into the sky. Good luck, crew, and have a safe flight!

Hello, friends, are you ready for some fun? Let's warm up our tongues with tongue twisters and rhymes. Say them slowly first, then faster and faster. Dana's dog dug deep down by the dusty door. Ten tall teachers took tea to Taraz on Tuesday. Funny Farida found five fresh figs in the fridge. Now a little rhyme. A cat in Aktau sat on a mat; she wore a red scarf and a very big hat. Big brown bees bake bread in Burabay. Silly Sasha sells seven shiny shells by the sea. Was that harder than you thought? Try again, and have fun!

Ladies and gentlemen, may I have your attention, please. This is an important announcement for passengers travelling to Istanbul on Steppe Air flight 427. Please note that the departure gate has been changed. The flight will now leave from Gate 12, not Gate 5. If you have already gone to Gate 5, please make your way to Gate 12 immediately. Boarding has already started. Passengers with small children and those who need extra help will be invited to board first, followed by business class. All other passengers will then be called by row number. Please have your boarding pass and passport ready. This is the final call for Steppe Air flight 427 to Istanbul. The gate will close at 10:45. Thank you.

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome aboard Flight 512 from Astana to Istanbul. My name is Dana, and I will be one of your flight attendants today. Before we take off, please make sure that your seat belt is fastened, your tray table is closed and your bags are stored in the overhead lockers or under the seat in front of you. If you are sitting next to an emergency exit, please read the safety card in your seat pocket. During the flight we will serve hot meals and drinks. If you need any help, just press the call button above your seat. We wish you a pleasant journey and thank you for flying with us.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Almaty Central Station. This is an announcement for passengers travelling to Astana. The 14:20 express to Astana has been delayed by about twenty minutes because of a technical problem on the line. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause. The train will now depart from platform 3, not platform 5 as shown on your tickets. If you have booked a seat, please check your carriage number before you get on. Passengers who need help with heavy luggage can ask any member of staff wearing a yellow jacket. Please mind the gap between the train and the platform when you board. Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the station. Thank you for travelling with Steppe Rail, and have a safe journey.

The next station is Abay. Please mind the gap between the train and the platform. Doors are closing. Please stand clear of the doors! Ladies and gentlemen, we apologise for the short delay at the last station. A passenger who felt unwell has been helped by our staff, and the train is now running normally again. We will arrive at Abay in about two minutes. If you want to change for the Green Line, please get off here and follow the signs. Passengers who are travelling to Raiymbek Batyr should stay on this train. If you see a bag that nobody is looking after, tell a member of staff straight away. Thank you for travelling with us, and have a nice day.

Hello, everyone, this is your driver speaking. Welcome on board the number 12 bus to Abay Square. If you haven't paid yet, please tap your travel card on the reader next to the door. Cash is no longer accepted on this route, so if you have forgotten your card, you can buy a ticket in the city transport app. The next stop is the Central Market. Please hold on to the handrail while the bus is moving. The seats at the front are kept for older passengers, parents with small children and anyone who needs them more than you do. If someone like that gets on, please offer them your seat. Ring the bell before your stop, not after it. Thank you, and enjoy your ride.

So, where are you from? Oh, Aktau! I have never been there, but my cousin says the sea is beautiful. We'll take Dostyk Avenue, because Abay is completely blocked at this time of day. If we had left half an hour earlier, we would be there already. Honestly, the traffic in this city has got much worse in the last few years. When I was a boy, I used to ride my bike down this street, and there were hardly any cars. Look on your right, those are the mountains. If you have some free time, take the cable car up to Kok Tobe in the evening. The view is amazing. There we are, the hotel is just round the corner. Enjoy your stay!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. Welcome aboard the ferry Caspian Star, sailing from the port of Aktau. We have just left the harbour, and our journey across the Caspian Sea should take about eighteen hours. The sea is calm tonight, but the wind is expected to get stronger after midnight, so please hold on to the rails when you walk on the open deck. Life jackets can be found under the beds in every cabin. If you hear seven short whistles and one long one, please go to your meeting point immediately and follow the crew. The restaurant on deck 4 is open until 22:00. Tonight's dinner is fresh fish which was caught this morning. Sleep well, and we'll see you at breakfast.

Good afternoon and welcome to the Grand Steppe Hotel. Your room is on the fourth floor, room four hundred and twelve, and the lifts are just behind me on the right. Breakfast is served from seven until half past ten in the restaurant on the ground floor. The swimming pool and the gym are open all day, and you can use them free of charge. Wi-Fi is available everywhere in the hotel; the password is written on your key card. If you would like a taxi or a table at a restaurant, just call reception and we will be happy to help. Enjoy your stay!

Right, everyone, gather round, please. Welcome to Charyn Canyon, one of the most amazing places in Kazakhstan. Some people call it the little brother of the Grand Canyon in America. The red rocks around you were shaped by wind and water over millions of years. This part is called the Valley of Castles, and I think you can see why. Have any of you been here before? No? Then you are in for a treat. We'll walk down to the river, which takes about forty minutes. The path is steep in places, so please watch your step and don't go near the edge. If you get tired, just let me know and we'll stop for a break. Make sure you drink plenty of water. Right, let's go!

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome aboard the Astana city tour. My name is Aigerim, and I'll be your guide today. Astana became the capital of Kazakhstan quite recently, and since then the city has grown incredibly fast. Many of the buildings you will see today were designed by famous architects from all over the world. On your left is the Baiterek tower. According to an old legend, a magic bird laid a golden egg at the top of a tall tree, and that's the story the tower tells. If you look to the right, you can see the river Ishim, which runs right through the city. In winter it freezes, and people go skating on it. Our first stop is in five minutes, so get your cameras ready!

Attention, shoppers! Thank you for choosing Dastan Home Store today. We are happy to tell you that our big autumn sale has just started. All winter coats, boots and scarves are now half price, so this is the perfect time to get ready for the cold weather. If you buy two kitchen items, you'll get the third one for free. Our customer service desk is next to the main entrance, where you can also pick up your online orders. Have you joined our loyalty club yet? Members get extra discounts every month and a small gift on their birthday. Please note that the store will close at 21:00 tonight. Customers are kindly asked to bring their baskets back to the checkout area. Happy shopping, and thank you!

Attention, shoppers. This is a lost and found announcement. A child's backpack has been found near the food court on the second floor. It is small and bright yellow, with a picture of a cartoon cat on the front. Inside, there is a pencil case and a book with the name Aruzhan written on it. If this backpack belongs to your child, please come to the information desk on the ground floor. We have also found a mobile phone which was left in the toilets next to the cinema. It has a black case with a silver star on the back. If you have lost this phone, you will be asked to describe it before you can collect it. Thank you for shopping at Sunrise Centre.

Good evening and welcome to Shanyrak, our little family restaurant! My name is Madina, and I'm the owner. My grandmother opened this place many years ago, and we still use a lot of her recipes. Let me tell you about the menu. Our most popular dish is beshbarmak, which is made with noodles cut by hand and tender lamb. If you prefer something lighter, try the vegetable soup or the fresh salad with herbs from our own garden. All our bread is baked here every morning. For dessert, I recommend the honey cake. To drink, we have hot tea with milk and homemade lemonade. If you have any allergies, just tell me and the cook will change the dish for you. Enjoy your meal!

Attention, please. Good morning and welcome to Ak Zhol Family Clinic. Please take a queue number from the machine by the entrance and wait until your number is shown on the screen. If you have booked an appointment online, you don't need a queue number. Just go straight to the reception desk and give your name. Patients who have a cough or a cold are kindly asked to wear a mask. Masks can be picked up at reception, and they are free. The pharmacy is located on the ground floor, next to the lifts, and it is open until 20:00. Please turn your phone to silent while you are waiting. Thank you for your patience, and we hope you feel better soon.

Good afternoon, readers, and welcome to the Central City Library of Shymkent. My name is Nurlan, and I'll show you around. This building was opened over fifty years ago, but it has recently been modernised. On the ground floor you'll find newspapers, magazines and the children's section. The quiet reading room is upstairs. Please keep your voice down there and switch your phone to silent. You can borrow up to five books for three weeks. If you return a book late, you will have to pay a small fine. Every Thursday evening we run a book club, which is free for all members. If you haven't signed up for a library card yet, come and see me at the desk. Happy reading!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Hall of Ancient Steppe Gold. The objects in this room were discovered by archaeologists in an old burial mound near the city of Turkistan. Look at this small gold deer. It was made by hand more than two thousand years ago, and yet every detail is still perfect. The people who lived here used to be nomads, so their jewellery was light and easy to carry. Now come over to this case. These clay pots were used for storing milk and grain. If you look carefully, you can still see fingerprints on them. Please don't touch the glass, and remember that flash photography isn't allowed in this hall. Now, follow me to the next room.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Aral Cinema. Tonight is a very special night, because you are among the first people in the country to see this film. It was shot entirely in Kazakhstan, in the mountains near Kolsay Lakes, and some of the actors are here with us in the hall. Before the film begins, please switch off your mobile phones or put them on silent. Recording the film is strictly forbidden. If you need to leave during the show, please use the exits at the side, which are marked with green lights. After the film, the director will answer your questions, so please stay in your seats. Popcorn and drinks are still available in the lobby. Sit back, relax and enjoy the show!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to tonight's concert at the Golden Dombyra Hall. We have a wonderful programme for you. In the first part, our national orchestra will play traditional music on the dombyra and the kobyz. After a short interval, a young singer from Shymkent will join us. She has won three international competitions this year, and tonight she is performing in Almaty for the very first time. Before we begin, please make sure your phones are switched off. Taking photos with a flash isn't allowed during the performance, because it disturbs the musicians. If you would like a programme, they are sold at the entrance. Drinks will be served in the hall during the interval. And now, please give a warm welcome to the orchestra!

Come here, my dear, come and try! These are the sweetest apples in the whole Green Bazaar. They were picked yesterday in my brother's garden near Almaty. Have you ever tasted a real Almaty apple? No? Then take one, it's free. Look at these apricots and raisins too. I dry them myself in the sun, without any sugar. If you buy a kilo of dried apricots, I'll give you a bag of walnuts as a present. And this bread came out of the oven an hour ago, smell it! My mother used to bake bread exactly like this. Prices? Don't worry, my prices are lower than anyone else's. For you, a special price, because you have a kind face. So, what would you like? Come back tomorrow, I'll be here!

Hello, boys and girls, and welcome to Almaty Zoo! My name is Timur, and I've worked as a keeper here for ten years. Our first stop today is the snow leopard. She is called Aisulu, and she was born here three years ago. Snow leopards live high up in the mountains of Kazakhstan, but there are not many of them left in the wild. Can you see her long tail? She uses it to keep warm, like a scarf! Next, we'll visit the camels. Camels have been used by people on the steppe for thousands of years. Now, please remember a few rules. Don't feed the animals, because our food can make them ill. Don't knock on the glass, and never put your hands through the fence. Ready? Let's go!

Good evening, and here is the news at seven. A new bridge over the Ural River has been opened in Atyrau. Local people say it will save them almost half an hour every day. In Almaty, a young doctor has saved the life of a passenger on a plane, after a man suddenly became ill during a flight from Astana. The airline has thanked her for her quick help. Scientists in Aktau have found that the number of seals in the Caspian Sea has risen for the first time in ten years. And finally, a school in Karaganda has set a new national record, after six hundred students read aloud together for one hour. That's all for now. Thank you for watching, and good night.

Good morning, and here's the weather forecast for Kazakhstan. It has been a cold week in the north, and I'm afraid it isn't going to get much warmer. In Astana, the day will start with thick fog, which should clear by lunchtime. Temperatures will stay below zero all day, so wrap up warm. Further south, the news is better. Almaty will enjoy bright sunshine for most of the day, although some clouds will come down from the mountains in the evening. If you live in Shymkent, you might need an umbrella, because heavy showers are expected in the afternoon. Out west in Aktau, it will be windy by the sea, so hold on to your hats. That's all from me. Have a lovely day, and see you tomorrow!

Good morning, you're listening to Steppe FM, and here's some news for everyone who wants to improve their English this summer. Have you ever felt shy when a tourist asked you for directions? If you could speak English with confidence, where would you travel? Sky Bridge Summer School can help you get there! All our courses are taught by friendly, experienced teachers, and classes are kept small, so everyone gets plenty of chances to speak. Many students who joined us last year have already passed their exams. And if you sign up before the end of May, you'll get a free speaking club. So don't wait! Call us today or visit our website. Sky Bridge Summer School: learn, speak, enjoy!

Hello and welcome back to Wander Steppe, the podcast for people who love to travel. I'm Dana, and I've just come back from the Kolsay lakes. I've never seen water so blue! For those of you who haven't been there yet, Kolsay is a group of three mountain lakes, about five hours' drive from Almaty. We stayed in a guest house in Saty village, which was run by a lovely family. On the second day, we hiked up to the second lake. It was hard work, but the view was worth it. Here are my tips. Set off early, because the paths get busy. Pack warm clothes, even in summer. And if you go in May, you might see snow! Stay with me, and I'll tell you everything.

And here we go, the second half is under way here in Almaty, and the crowd is already on its feet! It's still nil nil. Timur, who used to play for Shymkent, picks up the ball in the middle. He passes it out to Arman on the left. Arman runs past one defender, then another. He shoots! Oh, what a save by the goalkeeper! He has stopped three shots like that tonight. Corner to the home team. Nurlan takes it, the ball comes in high, and Ali heads it into the net! Goal! Listen to that noise! The fans have waited all season for a moment like this. If the team keeps playing like this, they will win the cup. What a night here in Almaty!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Central Stadium in Almaty! Tonight's match is between the Almaty Snow Leopards and the Astana Eagles, and it should be an exciting game. Both teams have won their last three matches, so everyone is expecting a great fight. Before the game starts, please listen carefully to some safety information. If you need to leave the stadium in an emergency, follow the green signs to the nearest exit. Fireworks and glass bottles are not allowed inside. Please don't stand on the seats or throw anything onto the pitch. Lost children will be taken to the information point under the south stand. Now, are you ready to make some noise? Let's give a big welcome to the players!

Here, on the endless steppe of central Kazakhstan, spring has finally arrived. For months, this land has been covered by snow and ice. Now the grass is turning green, and life is coming back. A herd of saiga antelope is moving slowly across the plain. These strange animals have lived here since the days of the mammoths. Their large noses work like filters, cleaning the dusty air before they breathe it. Not long ago, saigas almost disappeared. But thanks to the hard work of scientists and rangers, their numbers have grown again. Every spring, the herd travels hundreds of kilometres to find fresh grass. If the animals stay together, the young ones will be safer from wolves. Tonight, under a sky full of stars, a new calf will be born.

Hello and welcome back to Cooking with Dana! Today I'm going to show you how to make baursak, the soft fried bread that is served at every Kazakh celebration. My grandmother used to make it every Sunday, and the whole house smelled wonderful. First, mix warm milk with a little sugar and yeast, and leave it for ten minutes. Then add flour, an egg and a pinch of salt. Knead the dough until it is soft, and then cover it with a clean towel. If you put it somewhere warm, it will rise much faster. Now roll it out and cut it into small squares. Fry them in hot oil until they turn golden brown. Look at that! Serve them warm with tea and honey. See you next week!

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for coming. My name is Saule Bekova, and I am the spokesperson for the city of Shymkent. I'm pleased to announce that the new river park has finally been completed. Work started two years ago, and since then more than three thousand trees have been planted along the water. The park will be opened to the public next Saturday at 10:00. There will be free concerts, a play area for children and a cycle path that runs right through the city centre. Now, I believe there is a question from the local newspaper. Yes, you asked about parking. If the car park gets too full, extra buses will be provided from the main square. Thank you all, and we hope to see you there!

This is an emergency weather warning from the Almaty Region Weather Service. A strong storm is moving towards the city and is expected to arrive this evening at about 18:00. Winds of up to ninety kilometres an hour have been reported in the mountains, and heavy rain will follow. If you are outside, go indoors as soon as possible. Stay away from trees and old buildings, because branches and roofs may fall. If you have to drive, slow down and keep your lights on. Please don't go hiking tonight; several mountain roads have already been closed. Make sure your phone is charged and keep a torch close to hand. If you see a fallen power line, don't touch it. Stay safe, and keep listening for updates.

Good morning, students and teachers. This is your deputy head, Mr Serikbayev, with today's announcements. First, please note that the timetable has been changed for this week. On Wednesday, the last two lessons will be replaced by a meeting in the main hall, which starts at 13:30. Second, the school science fair is coming up on Friday. If you haven't registered your project yet, please see Ms Akhmetova in room 214 before the end of the day. Third, a blue sports bag has been found in the gym. If it's yours, you can pick it up from reception. Finally, a reminder for the football team: training has been moved to Thursday because of the weather. Have a great day, and don't forget your homework!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome back! Please sit down and put your phones away. Today we're going to talk about cities of the future. First, I'll show you a short video about a smart city that was built near the sea a few years ago. Then you'll work in groups of three. Your task is to design a city in Kazakhstan that people will want to live in twenty years from now. Think about transport, parks, schools and energy. If you finish early, you can draw a map of your city. At the end, each group will give a short presentation. I know some of you get nervous when you speak in front of the class, but remember: we've all been there. Right, let's get started!

Good morning, and thank you for inviting me today. My name is Arman Zhaksybekov, and I'm from Pavlodar, although I have lived in Astana for the last five years. I studied tourism at university, and since then I have worked as a manager at a small hotel near the river. My job involves organising tours, dealing with guests who have problems and training new staff. I used to be quite shy, but working with people from many countries has changed that. I'm applying for this position because your company is growing fast, and I'd like to take on more responsibility. If I'm offered the job, I'll bring energy, patience and plenty of good ideas. Thank you, and I'm happy to answer your questions.

Good morning, Aigerim, and welcome to the team! We're really happy you've joined us. Let me show you around. This is the main office, where most of us work. Your desk is next to the window, and your computer has already been set up for you. This is Nurlan, who looks after our clients, and that's Madina, who is in charge of the design team. If you have any problems with your computer, ask Arman; he knows everything about technology. The kitchen is at the end of the corridor, so feel free to make tea or coffee whenever you like. We usually have lunch together at 1:00, and today it's on me! Right, let's get you settled in. Welcome aboard!

Good afternoon, colleagues, and thank you for joining me. Today I'd like to present the results of our online delivery project, which was launched in Karaganda six months ago. Let's start with the good news. Since March, our number of customers has doubled, and most orders are now delivered in less than an hour. Our new app has been downloaded by thousands of people, and the feedback has been very positive. However, we have also faced some problems. Some drivers have complained about long working hours, and our costs have gone up. So what are the next steps? First, we'll hire more drivers before winter. Second, we'll open a second warehouse. If everything goes well, we'll expand to Aktobe next year. Any questions?

Hi Madina, it's Dana. Sorry I missed your call; I was on the bus and couldn't hear a thing. Listen, I've got some news about our trip to Burabay. The guesthouse that we booked has just phoned me. Apparently a pipe has broken in our room, so they've offered us a bigger room with a lake view at no extra cost! Isn't that great? The only thing is, we'll have to check in after 15:00 instead of noon. So I was thinking, if we leave Astana a bit later, we could stop for lunch on the way. What do you think? Oh, and could you bring your camera? Mine was left at my sister's house. Call me back when you get this. Bye!

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Green Steppe Conference here in Astana. It's wonderful to see so many people in this hall. Some of you have travelled from Aktau, others from Semey, and a few guests have flown in from abroad. Thank you for coming. Ten years ago, this event was organised by a small group of students who cared about the environment. Today it has become one of the largest meetings of its kind in Central Asia. Over the next two days, you will hear from scientists, farmers and young inventors. If we work together, we can find answers that nobody has found alone. So please ask questions, share your ideas and make new friends. Let's begin!

Dear teachers, parents and, of course, my fellow graduates, good evening. It's an honour to speak to you tonight. When we first walked into this school eleven years ago, most of us were tiny, nervous children who were holding our mothers' hands. Look at us now! We have learned so much, not only from books, but also from each other. I remember the trip to Kolsay Lakes when our bus broke down, and we sang songs for three hours in the rain. Those are the moments that I'll never forget. Our teachers have always believed in us, even when we didn't believe in ourselves. Thank you for your patience. Wherever we go next, we'll carry this school in our hearts. Congratulations, everyone!

Good afternoon, judges, opponents and audience. My name is Aigerim, and our team is speaking for the motion that school uniforms should be kept. Let me explain why. First, uniforms make life easier. If students wear the same clothes, nobody is judged for what they can or cannot afford. Second, uniforms save time. Many parents have told us that mornings used to be stressful, but now there are no arguments about what to wear. Third, a uniform helps students feel part of a team, especially at sports events and competitions. Our opponents will say that uniforms stop people from showing their personality. However, personality is shown through ideas and actions, not through jackets. For these reasons, we strongly support the motion. Thank you.

Your Honour, thank you for giving me the opportunity to speak. I represent Mr Nurlan Abenov, who owns a flat on the third floor of a building in Almaty. Since last September, my client has been disturbed almost every night by loud music from the restaurant below. The music often continues until two in the morning. My client has complained to the owner several times, and a formal letter was sent in November, but nothing has changed. The restaurant's licence clearly states that music must be turned off at 23:00. If the court agrees, we are asking for the restaurant to follow these rules and to install better sound protection. My client is not trying to close the business; he simply wants to sleep. Thank you.

Hi everyone! My name is Timur, and I'm sixteen years old. I was born in Kostanay, but my family moved to Almaty when I was ten, so I've lived here for six years now. I live with my parents, my grandmother and my little sister, Aruzhan, who is always asking me to help with her homework. Our flat is near the mountains, and on clear days the view is amazing. In my free time I play basketball, and I've recently taken up photography. I used to play the dombra, but I gave it up because I didn't have enough time. Next year I'm going to finish school, and if I pass my exams, I'd like to study engineering. Nice to meet you all!

Good evening, everyone! Could I have your attention for a moment, please? For those who don't know me, I'm Ruslan, the groom's older brother. First of all, thank you all for coming tonight. Some of you have travelled a long way from Taraz and Kyzylorda, and it means a lot to our family. I've known Daniyar all his life, and I can honestly say that he has never been so happy. When he first met Zhanna at university, he couldn't stop talking about her. Zhanna, you have brought so much joy into our home, and we're proud to welcome you to the family. So, please raise your glasses. To Daniyar and Zhanna: may your life together be full of love and laughter!

So, you want to hear about my summer holiday? Okay, it was quite an adventure! In July, my cousins and I went to Aktau, on the Caspian Sea. We had never been there before, and honestly, we didn't know what to expect. On the first day, we hired bikes and rode along the coast. The water was so clear that we could see fish swimming near the rocks. On the third day, we took a tour to some amazing white canyons, which were formed millions of years ago. Our guide told us that the whole area used to be under the sea. The only problem was the heat; my phone stopped working in the sun! If I get the chance, I'll definitely go back next year.

Okay, everyone, come and sit around the fire. Make sure you've got your blankets, because it gets cold in the mountains at night. First of all, well done, all of you! Today we have walked almost fifteen kilometres, and nobody gave up, not even when it started to rain. I was really impressed. Now, about tomorrow. We'll get up at 07:00, have breakfast and then set off for Kolsay Lake. If the weather is good, we'll go out on the boats in the afternoon. A few rules before bed: nobody leaves the camp alone, torches must be kept next to your sleeping bags, and all food must be put away, because animals can smell it. Right, who wants to tell the first story?

I love walking in the Central Park on a Sunday morning, especially in autumn. The paths are covered with yellow and red leaves, and the air smells fresh and slightly sweet. Over there, an old man is feeding the pigeons, which seem to know him very well. A group of students is jogging past, laughing and chatting. Have you noticed how quiet the city feels from here? The noise of the traffic just fades away. In spring, this park is completely different. The apple trees are in flower, and families come here to have picnics on the grass. I've walked here every weekend since I moved to Almaty, and I never get bored. If you're ever in the city, come and join me!

Dear diary, it's Saturday, and it has been raining since early morning. I was going to meet Aliya in the city centre, but she called and told me that her bus was cancelled. So I've decided to stay at home and enjoy a lazy day. I've made a big pot of tea with milk, just like my grandmother used to make, and I've found my thickest blanket. Right now I'm sitting by the window, listening to the rain on the roof. It's strange, but I find the sound so relaxing. I've already read half of a mystery novel, and I'm dying to find out how it ends. Later I might bake some baursaks if there's enough flour. Honestly, rainy days aren't so bad after all.

Right, everyone, are you ready? Let's go! Turn the music up! We're going to start by warming up, so march on the spot. Lift those knees! Good. Now swing your arms forward and back. Okay, now we're moving on to squats. Feet apart, back straight, and down, and up. Down, and up! Keep going! Next, ten jumping jacks. If you feel tired, slow down, but don't stop moving. If your knees hurt, just step to the side instead of jumping. Remember, nobody here is judging you. We've all been beginners! Take a quick drink of water. Now lunges, left leg first. Breathe out as you push up. You're doing brilliantly! Last one, and hold it! Fantastic work, everyone. Give yourselves a big round of applause!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome! Before we set off, please listen carefully, because your safety is the most important thing today. Our route goes up the valley to a small lake. The walk takes about six hours. It has been sunny this morning, but in the mountains the weather can change very quickly. If it starts to rain, put on your jacket straight away. Have you all brought at least two litres of water? Please drink a little every half hour, even if you don't feel thirsty. Most importantly, stay together.
