I'll walk at the front, and Arman will be at the back. If you need to stop, tell one of us. Never leave the path. Right, if there are no questions, let's go!

This is Baikonur Mission Control. All systems are go. The rocket has been fuelled, and the crew of three is ready on board. Five, four, three, two, one, lift off! And there it goes, rising slowly into the clear morning sky. The engines are working perfectly. In just under nine minutes, the spacecraft will reach orbit. Commander Aidarov, can you hear us? The commander has just reported that the crew are feeling fine and the view of the Earth is incredible. Wonderful news. If everything goes to plan, the crew will dock with the space station in about six hours. Their mission will last six months, and dozens of experiments will be carried out on board. Good luck, crew, and safe travels!

Welcome to Tongue Twister Corner! Are you ready to warm up your mouth? Let's begin slowly, and then speed up. Six silly seagulls sat on six salty stones by the Caspian Sea. Try it again, faster! Next one: Dana's daughter drew a dozen dancing dolphins on a dusty door. Good job! Now here's a little rhyme for you. A cat from Astana once lost her red hat; she searched every shop, then sat down on a mat. Here's a tricky one: fresh fried fish from five fast fishermen filled five full plates. And finally: if Timur's tiny tortoise has taken two tomatoes, how many tomatoes has Timur's tiny tortoise taken? Say it three times without stopping. Well done, everybody! You've been brilliant today.

Ladies and gentlemen, welcome to Almaty International Airport. This is an announcement for passengers travelling on Steppe Air Flight 427 to Aktau. We regret to inform you that the departure has been delayed, as the aircraft is still being cleaned and refuelled after a late arrival from Astana. Boarding is now expected to begin at 10:45 from Gate 12. If you had checked in online, you would already have received a message with this information, so please make sure your phone is switched on. Passengers who have not yet passed through security are kindly asked to do so without delay. This is the final call for passenger Nurlan Seitkali, travelling to Aktau. Your bags have already been loaded, so you must have checked in, but the flight is now being held for you. Please proceed immediately to Gate 12. Thank you for flying with Steppe Air.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome on board Silk Wing Flight 215 from Astana to Shymkent. My name is Aigerim, and I am your senior cabin attendant today. Our flight time will be approximately one hour and forty minutes. Before we take off, please direct your attention to the screens, where the safety demonstration will be shown. Even if you fly with us every week, we would ask you to watch it carefully, because your nearest exit may be behind you. Please make sure that your seat belt is fastened, your seat back is upright and your tray table is stowed. Once we have reached cruising altitude, a light meal will be served, followed by hot and cold drinks. The captain has informed us that the weather in Shymkent is sunny and warm. We will make another announcement before we begin our descent. Sit back, relax and enjoy the flight.

Ladies and gentlemen, we regret to announce that the 14:20 service from Almaty to Astana has been delayed by approximately three hours. We apologise for the inconvenience this will cause. We have been informed that a freight train broke down in the Karaganda region this morning, and as a result, the line has been blocked in both directions. Engineers are working on the track, but it must have been more seriously damaged than was first thought. Passengers who have already bought tickets are entitled to full compensation. Refunds can be requested at the ticket office or through our mobile application. Alternatively, you may travel on the 15:40 service, which will depart from platform 6 and arrive in Astana this evening. Free drinks and snacks are being offered in the waiting hall for anyone affected. Had we known about the problem sooner, you would have been informed earlier. Thank you for your patience and understanding.

Welcome aboard. This train is bound for Moskva. The next station is Abay. Please mind the gap between the train and the platform. Passengers are reminded that the doors close automatically, so please do not try to board once the warning signal has sounded. Attention, please. The escalators at Abay station are being repaired this week, and passengers are advised to use the lifts instead. If you were planning to change to a bus at Abay, you might find it quicker to get off at Baikonur. Please be considerate of other passengers. Priority seats should be offered to elderly people, pregnant women and passengers with small children. Large bags must not be placed on seats, and eating is not allowed on board. If you notice an unattended item, it should be reported to a member of staff immediately. This is Abay. Thank you for travelling with us.

Good morning, and welcome on board the number twelve bus to Shymkent city centre. This is your driver speaking. The next stop is Central Park. Please remember that fares are no longer paid in cash; tickets must be bought with a travel card or through the city transport app before you sit down. If you haven't validated your card, an inspector could fine you. Passengers are kindly asked to move towards the back of the bus so that more people can get on. The seats near the front have been reserved for elderly and disabled passengers. Next stop, Ordabasy Square. Please hold on tight, because the road near the market is being repaired and it may be a bit bumpy. If I had known about the roadworks earlier, I would have taken a different route. Thank you for travelling with us, and have a great day.

So, you're going up to Kok Tobe? Good choice. You must have arrived recently, because you've definitely got that tourist look, no offence! I've been driving a taxi in Almaty for twelve years, so I know every shortcut in this city. Normally I'd take Abay Avenue, but it's being dug up again, so we'll go along Dostyk instead. If you'd called me an hour earlier, we would have been stuck in the morning rush for ages. People say the traffic here is getting worse every year, and honestly, I agree. Mind you, the mountains make up for it. Look over there, you can see the peaks are already covered in snow. My cousin claims that the best views are from Medeu, but I reckon Kok Tobe is better at sunset. Ah, here we are. That'll be two thousand tenge. Enjoy the view, and don't leave your phone on the back seat!

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, this is your captain speaking. Welcome aboard the Silver Gull. We left the port of Aktau about an hour ago, and we are now sailing west across the Caspian Sea. The weather is pleasant, although the wind has been getting stronger, so some movement of the ship may be felt this evening. Before we continue, I must ask for your attention for a short safety briefing. A lifejacket can be found in the wardrobe of every cabin. If you hear seven short blasts followed by one long blast, please put on your lifejacket and go directly to your muster station, which is shown on the back of your cabin door. Children must be supervised on the open decks at all times, and nobody should climb on the railings. Dinner will be served from 19:00 in the main restaurant. Thank you, and enjoy your voyage.

Good evening, and welcome to the Burabay Lakeside Hotel. My name is Madina. You must be Mr Timur Akhmetov; we've been expecting you. Your booking has been confirmed for three nights, and you've been given room 214 on the second floor, which overlooks the lake. Here is your key card. Breakfast is served in the Pine Restaurant from 7:00 until 10:30, and if you prefer, it can be brought to your room for a small extra charge. The spa and swimming pool are open until 22:00, and towels are provided by the pool. I should mention that the sauna is being renovated at the moment, so unfortunately it can't be used. Had you arrived last week, you could have enjoyed it! Reception is open around the clock, so if you need anything at all, just dial zero. Enjoy your stay with us.

Welcome to Charyn Canyon, one of the most spectacular natural wonders of Kazakhstan. The canyon stretches for about one hundred and fifty kilometres, and some of its walls rise more than three hundred metres above the river. The part we are standing in is known as the Valley of Castles, because the red rock formations look like ancient towers and walls. Scientists believe these rocks have been shaped by wind and water for over twelve million years. Please stay on the marked path, drink plenty of water and keep an eye on the time, as we will meet back at the bus in exactly two hours.

Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome aboard our Astana city tour. My name is Arman, and I'll be your guide for the next two hours. If you look to your left, you'll see the Baiterek Tower. It was designed to represent an old legend about a magic bird that laid a golden egg in the branches of the tree of life. The observation deck offers a fantastic view of the whole city. Not so long ago, this entire area was open steppe, and it's hard to believe that the city was only declared the capital in the late nineties. Coming up on the right is the Hazret Sultan Mosque, which is said to be one of the largest in Central Asia. Our next stop is the Palace of Peace and Reconciliation, the famous pyramid. If you had visited in winter, you would have seen how beautifully its lights reflect off the snow. Thank you!

Attention, shoppers! Welcome to Dala Home Market, your favourite store for everything you need at home. We are delighted to announce that our autumn sale has officially begun. All kitchen appliances have been reduced by up to thirty per cent, and every second pair of winter boots is half price. Don't miss out, because these offers are only valid while stocks last. Customers with a loyalty card will also receive double points on all purchases made today. If you haven't signed up yet, you can register at any till in less than a minute. Last weekend, our wool blankets were sold out within hours, so if you'd like one, we strongly recommend heading to aisle seven now. Please note that the store will be open until 23:00 tonight and from 8:00 tomorrow morning. Should you need any help, our friendly staff will be happy to assist you. Thank you for shopping with us!

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Esil Plaza Shopping Centre. Fashion stores can be found on the ground and first floors, while the food court and cinema are located on the third floor. A new children's play area has recently been opened next to the food court. Could the parents of a little boy called Ali please come to the information desk on the ground floor? He has told our staff that he lost sight of his mother near the toy shop. Don't worry, he's perfectly safe and is being looked after by our team. We would also like to inform you that a black backpack has been handed in to lost and found. It must have been left on a bench near the fountain. Don't forget our live music show, which starts at 18:00 on the central stage. Please note that the centre closes at 22:00. Thank you for visiting us.

Good evening, and welcome to the Sary Arka Tea House! Please take a seat wherever you like. I'm Dana, the owner, and I'll be looking after you tonight. Let me tell you about some of our specialities. Our beshbarmak is prepared according to my grandmother's recipe, and the meat is cooked slowly for over four hours. If you prefer something lighter, I'd recommend the pumpkin manti, which are steamed and served with sour cream. All our bread is baked here every morning. For dessert, you really must try the baursaks with honey; one of our regulars told me last week that they were the best he had ever eaten. Tea is served the traditional way, with milk, in small bowls. Had you come yesterday, you could have tried our camel milk ice cream, but I'm afraid it's sold out. Take your time, and just call me when you're ready to order. Enjoy!

Good morning, and welcome to Nur Family Clinic. Please take a ticket from the machine by the entrance and wait until your number appears on the screen. Patients who have booked an appointment online are asked to check in at the first window. Today, appointments are running about twenty minutes late, as two of our doctors have been called away to an emergency. We apologise for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience. If you had booked through our app, you would have received a text message about the delay. Please remember that masks should be worn in the waiting area if you have a cough or a cold. Mobile phones must be switched to silent, and calls should be made outside. If you are unable to attend, your appointment must be cancelled at least one day in advance. Aruzhan Bekova, please come to room 3. Thank you.

Good afternoon, and welcome to the Shymkent City Library. On this floor, you'll find fiction, which has been arranged alphabetically by author. Upstairs is the reference section, where books cannot be borrowed but can be read in the study area. Please note that eating is not permitted anywhere in the building, although drinks in closed bottles are allowed. Phones should be kept on silent. Members can borrow up to five books at a time for three weeks. If a book is returned late, a small fine will be charged. One reader told me she hadn't known about the fine, but it was clearly printed on her card! This Saturday, a reading club will be held in the children's corner, and a local author has been invited to talk about her new novel. If you had joined us last month, you would have met a poet from Taraz. The library closes at 19:00. Happy reading!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Hall of the Ancient Steppe. Please gather round this glass case. What you can see here is a golden belt buckle, which was discovered by archaeologists near Lake Balkhash in the last century. It is believed to have belonged to a nomadic warrior, and judging by the fine decoration, he can't have been an ordinary soldier. He must have been a leader of some kind. Now, follow me into the next room. These felt carpets were made by hand over two hundred years ago. The bright colours were produced using natural dyes from plants and roots. Experts say that if the carpets had been kept in a damp place, they would have been destroyed long ago. Please don't touch the exhibits, and remember that flash photography is not allowed. Our tour will finish in the gift shop, where postcards and books can be bought. Thank you for listening.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the premiere of Wind over Kolsay at the Aral Cinema Hall. Before the film begins, I'd like to say a few words. This film was shot entirely in the Almaty region, and most of the scenes were filmed at sunrise, so the crew had to get up at four every morning. The director told me she would never have finished on time if the local villagers hadn't helped with horses and food. After the screening, the director and the lead actors will be invited onto the stage for a short question and answer session. Please make sure your phones are switched off or set to silent, as any light from a screen can be very distracting. Recording of any kind is strictly prohibited. Emergency exits are located on both sides of the hall. Now sit back, relax and enjoy the film.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Silk Road Concert Hall for tonight's performance of Songs of the Great Steppe. We are honoured to have the Burabay Chamber Orchestra with us, along with the young dombra player Aruzhan Tulegenova, who was awarded first prize at the national competition this spring. The programme will be divided into two parts. In the first part, traditional kuis will be performed, and after an interval of twenty minutes, the orchestra will play modern works inspired by Kazakh folk music. We kindly ask you to switch off your mobile phones now. Photographs and recordings are not permitted. Latecomers will only be admitted at a suitable break. Our conductor told me earlier that, had he not fallen in love with the dombra as a child, he would have become a doctor. Lucky for us! Please welcome them with a big round of applause!

Come closer, my friend, come and have a look! Welcome to the Green Bazaar, the best market in Almaty, and this is the best stall in it! These apples were picked only yesterday in the foothills, just outside the city. Go on, try one. Sweet, aren't they? My grandfather always said that if Almaty hadn't been famous for its apples, it would have been given a different name! Now, look at this dried fruit. The apricots come from Shymkent, and they've been dried naturally in the sun, with no sugar added. The raisins and figs are excellent too. And here is fresh bread, baked this morning in a clay oven. You must be hungry after walking around all day. Today, I can give you a kilo of apricots for three thousand tenge, but only because you're smiling. If you take two kilos, I'll throw in a bag of walnuts for free. Deal? Wonderful, enjoy!

Hello, everyone, and welcome to the mountain animals section of our zoo. My name is Ruslan, and I've been looking after these animals for eight years. Now, if you look up at those rocks, you'll see our snow leopard, Aisulu. She was rescued as a cub in the Tien Shan mountains, where she had been found alone and very weak. She must be watching us right now, but her grey coat makes her almost invisible. Snow leopards are rarely seen in the wild, and sadly, they are still being hunted illegally. Over here are our saiga antelopes. A few decades ago, they were nearly wiped out, and if they hadn't been protected, they might have disappeared completely. Please remember a few simple rules. The animals must not be fed, and you shouldn't tap on the glass or shout. Feeding time is at 15:00, so do come back and watch. Thank you!

Good evening, this is the eight o'clock news. A new high-speed railway connecting the capital with the southern regions has officially opened today, cutting the journey time almost in half. Officials say the project will create thousands of jobs and make travel more affordable for families and students. Meanwhile, scientists at a local university have developed an app that helps farmers predict weather changes with remarkable accuracy. And finally, in sport, our national team has qualified for the international championship after a dramatic victory in the final minutes of last night's match.

Good evening, and here is the weather forecast for tomorrow. A cold front, which has been moving in from Siberia, is expected to bring a sharp drop in temperatures across the north of the country. In Astana, skies will be grey for most of the day, with strong winds and light snow, and temperatures will barely rise above minus five. Drivers are advised to take extra care, as roads could become icy by the evening. Meanwhile, the south will stay much milder. Almaty can look forward to a sunny morning, although clouds may build up over the mountains in the afternoon. Shymkent will be the warmest place, with a pleasant fourteen degrees. Out west in Aktau, it will be breezy along the Caspian coast. Yesterday, many people in Karaganda were caught in heavy rain; had the warning come earlier, fewer of them would have been surprised. So, wrap up warm, and have a lovely evening.

Are you tired of spending every weekend stuck in the city? Then it's time you discovered Kolsay Eco Lodge, the perfect escape in the heart of the mountains! Imagine waking up to birdsong, crystal clear lakes and the smell of pine trees. Our cosy wooden cabins have been built by local craftsmen, and every meal is prepared with fresh produce from nearby farms. Last summer, one of our guests told us that if she had known about us earlier, she would have come years ago. Spend your days hiking, horse riding or simply relaxing by the fire. This month only, families who book three nights will get the fourth night completely free! But hurry, because our autumn dates are being booked up fast. Don't wait until it's too late. Call us today or book online, and give yourself the break you deserve. Kolsay Eco Lodge: nature is waiting for you!

Hello and welcome to Steppe Talk, the podcast where we explore the habits that shape our everyday lives. I'm your host, Dana Seitkali, and today's episode is all about sleep. Recently, a survey was carried out among students in Almaty, and the results were rather surprising. Most of them admitted that their phones were kept beside their pillows every single night. If they had switched them off an hour earlier, they might have slept far better. My guest today is a doctor from Astana who has been studying sleep for over ten years. She told me before we started recording that most of us must be underestimating how much rest our brains really need. So, whether you're a night owl or an early bird, stay with us. By the end of this episode, you'll have at least three practical tips to try tonight. Let's get started!

And here we go, the second half is under way here at the Astana Arena, and what a night it's turning out to be! The home side, the Steppe Eagles, are trailing by a single goal, and the pressure is clearly building. Nurlan Abenov picks up the ball on the left, he skips past one defender, then another! He crosses, and it's headed just wide! Oh, he must be furious with himself. If that had gone in, the whole stadium would have exploded. The coach has been told by the referee to stay inside his area, and he doesn't look pleased about it. Meanwhile, the visitors from Shymkent are defending deep, clearly hoping to hold on. Five minutes remain. Corner kick! Timur rises highest, and it's in! It's in! The Eagles have equalised at the very last moment, and the fans are absolutely ecstatic! What a finish!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to the Astana Arena for tonight's cup final between Almaty City and Shymkent United! The gates were opened two hours ago, and the stadium has already been filled almost to capacity. Before kick off, a few important announcements must be made. Fans with tickets for the north stand are kindly asked to use Entrances 3 and 4, as the main entrance has been closed for safety reasons. Bags will be checked at every gate, so please be patient with our stewards. Fireworks, glass bottles and flags on long poles are strictly forbidden. If you need any assistance during the match, our staff in yellow jackets will be happy to help. Should an emergency occur, please follow their instructions and leave calmly by the nearest exit. However tense the game becomes, respect is expected from everyone. Enjoy the match responsibly, and may the best team win!

Here, on the endless grasslands of the Kazakh steppe, spring has finally arrived. For weeks, the skies have been watched by scientists, and now the first travellers are appearing on the horizon. These are demoiselle cranes, the smallest cranes in the world, and they have just completed an extraordinary journey from Africa and South Asia. Some of them must have flown over the Himalayas, where the air is thin and freezing. Had they not built up enough fat during the winter, they would never have survived the crossing. Their arrival is announced by loud, musical calls that can be heard from far away. Soon, pairs will be formed and elaborate dances will be performed, with jumps, bows and wings spread wide. However, life here is not easy. Nests are built on the ground, so eggs can easily be taken by foxes. Nevertheless, year after year, the cranes return, and the steppe comes alive again.

Good evening, and welcome back to the grand final of Kitchen Stars Kazakhstan! Only three chefs are left, and tonight one of them will be crowned champion. Aigerim, Timur and Madina, you have done brilliantly to get this far. Now, here's the challenge. You'll be given ninety minutes to create a menu of three courses inspired by your childhood. Every dish must include at least one ingredient that is grown in Kazakhstan. Your mystery box has already been placed on your bench, but it mustn't be opened until I say so. Your food will be judged on taste, presentation and creativity, and points will be deducted if anything is served late. Remember, last week a dish was almost perfect, but it was sent back because the meat was undercooked. Had it been cooked properly, that chef would have won. So, be careful, stay calm and trust your instincts. Chefs, your time starts now!

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for coming. I'm pleased to announce that a new cycling lane will be built along Abay Avenue, connecting the city centre with the university district. Construction is expected to begin in April and should be completed by the end of the summer. I am aware that this project has been criticised by some drivers and shop owners. It has been suggested that traffic will get worse and that customers will stop visiting local shops. However, similar lanes were introduced in many European cities, and in most cases, business improved. If we had invested in cycling ten years ago, our air would be much cleaner today. I was asked yesterday whether parking spaces would be lost. Yes, a small number will be removed, although new parking will be provided on nearby streets. We believe this is a step towards a healthier city. Now, I'm happy to take your questions.

Good afternoon, you're listening to City Radio Almaty, and this is an urgent warning from the Regional Emergency Weather Service. A severe thunderstorm is expected to reach the city by 18:00 this evening. Heavy rain, strong winds and large hailstones have been forecast, and flooding is likely in low areas near the rivers. Residents are strongly advised to stay indoors and keep away from windows. Loose objects on balconies should be secured or brought inside, because they could easily be blown away. If you have to go out, avoid parking under trees, which might fall in the high winds. Drivers are asked to reduce their speed, since visibility will be poor and the roads may become dangerous. Several mountain roads, including the route to Medeu, have already been closed. As a result, travellers are recommended to postpone any unnecessary journeys until tomorrow morning. Updates will be broadcast every thirty minutes. Stay safe, and stay tuned.

Good morning, students and staff, this is your morning announcement. Please listen carefully, as several changes have been made to today's timetable. Due to a heating problem, the science labs on the second floor have been closed, so all chemistry lessons will be held in the library instead. Secondly, the annual charity fair, which had been planned for Friday, has been postponed until next Wednesday. We have been informed by the organisers that more stalls are needed, so if your class would like to take part, please speak to Ms Akhmetova by the end of the week. A reminder to all senior students: your university application forms must be submitted no later than Monday. Forms that arrive late will not be accepted, I'm afraid. Finally, the bus to the volleyball tournament in Shymkent will leave from the main entrance at 7:30 tomorrow, so please don't be late. Thank you, and have a productive day!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome back. Please put your phones away and open your notebooks, because we have a busy lesson ahead of us. Today we're going to focus on reported speech, which, I know, some of you found a bit tricky last week. First, we'll warm up with a short discussion. Then I'll play you an interview with a young chef from Aktau, and your task will be to report what she said to your partner without looking at the transcript. After that, you'll write a short summary for homework. Now, I can see some worried faces. Don't panic! If you hadn't made those mistakes last week, we wouldn't be practising this today, and mistakes are exactly how we learn. By the end of the lesson, I promise, you'll be reporting conversations like professional journalists. Right, let's begin with a question: what's the most interesting thing someone told you this weekend?

Good afternoon, and thank you for inviting me to this interview. My name is Aigerim Nurpeisova, and I'm applying for the position of marketing coordinator. I graduated from university in Almaty with a degree in business, and since then I've been working for a small travel agency in Astana. In my current role, I'm responsible for planning social media campaigns and dealing with clients from all over Central Asia. Last year, our tours to Charyn Canyon were promoted by my team, and bookings increased significantly. Honestly, if I hadn't taken a risk with a new video format, we might have lost several important partners. I'm particularly interested in your company because you've recently expanded into international markets, and I'd love to be part of that growth. I'm a fast learner, I work well under pressure, and I speak Kazakh, Russian and English fluently. I'd be happy to answer any questions you may have. Thank you.

Welcome to the team, Arman! We're really glad you've joined us. Let me give you a quick tour before your first meeting. This is the main area where most of the design team sits. Your desk is the one by the window, and your laptop has already been set up by our IT department. Over there is the kitchen; coffee and tea are free, but please wash your own cup, or Madina will remind you, very politely. Now, about your tasks. For the first two weeks, you'll be shadowing Ruslan, who has been working on our Shymkent project since spring. He'll show you how reports are prepared and submitted. Don't worry if everything seems overwhelming at first. You must be feeling a little nervous, and that's completely normal. If you have any questions, my door is always open. Right, let's go and meet everyone. They've even ordered a cake for you!

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining this meeting. Today, I'll be presenting the results for the third quarter, and I'll also be honest about the challenges we've faced. Let's start with the good news. Sales of our Steppe Fresh juice range rose by twelve per cent, mainly because a new distribution centre was opened in Shymkent. In addition, our online orders have been growing since the new website was launched in July. However, profits were lower than we had expected. Transport costs increased sharply, and as a result, our margins were reduced. Two large orders were also cancelled by a client in Astana, who said that our delivery times had been too long. Looking back, if we had hired more drivers earlier, those orders might not have been lost. So, our main priority for the next quarter is logistics. On the next slide, I'll show you how we plan to fix it.

Hi Aruzhan, it's Timur. Sorry I missed your call earlier; I was stuck in a meeting that went on forever. Anyway, I'm calling about our trip to Burabay next weekend. I spoke to the hotel this morning, and they told me that our booking had been confirmed, but the lake view rooms had already been taken. They said they could offer us two rooms facing the forest instead, which, honestly, might be even quieter. Also, Dana mentioned that she couldn't come on Saturday because her sister's wedding has been moved. If we'd known earlier, we could have changed the dates. So, what do you think? Should we go on Sunday instead and stay an extra night? Could you let me know by tomorrow evening, because the hotel needs an answer before Friday? Oh, and don't forget your hiking boots this time! Okay, speak soon. Bye!

Good morning, everyone, and thank you so much for being here. I'd like to begin with a confession. Five years ago, I was told by a teacher that I was simply too old to learn English. I was nearly forty, and I believed her. If I had listened to her, I wouldn't be standing on this stage today. The truth is that I failed many times. I mixed up my tenses, I forgot words in the middle of sentences, and once I accidentally told my new boss in a meeting that I was pregnant instead of prepared. Everyone laughed, and eventually, so did I. However, every mistake taught me something that no textbook could have taught me. Adults are often afraid of looking foolish, although that fear is exactly what stops them from improving. So today, I'd like to talk about failure, not as the end of learning, but as the beginning. Shall we start?

Good evening, teachers, families and, of course, my fellow graduates. It's a huge honour to be standing here tonight. Four years ago, when we first walked through the doors of this university in Almaty, most of us had no idea what lay ahead. We were nervous, we got lost in the corridors, and some of us, I won't mention names, were late for almost every lecture. And yet, look at us now. We have been challenged, encouraged and, occasionally, completely exhausted. If our teachers hadn't believed in us, many of us wouldn't be wearing these gowns today. So, to every professor who stayed late to answer our questions: thank you. To our parents, who supported us through every single exam: thank you. Wherever life takes us next, whether it's Astana, Aktau or the other side of the world, let's remember where it all began. Congratulations, everyone. We did it!

Thank you, Madam Chair, honourable judges and members of the opposition. Today's motion is that online learning is just as effective as learning in a classroom, and my team strongly supports it. Let me begin with a simple fact. Over the past few years, millions of students have been taught online, and many of them have achieved excellent results. Consider a student living in a small village near Kolsay. Ten years ago, she would have had to move to Almaty to study with a top teacher. Today, she can attend the same lessons from her kitchen table. Our opponents will argue that students lose motivation at home. However, motivation depends on how a course is designed, not on the walls around us. Furthermore, online platforms allow learners to replay lessons as many times as they need. In conclusion, we believe that where you learn matters far less than how you learn. Thank you.

Your Honour, thank you for the opportunity to present my client's case. My client, Mr Bekzat Omarov, has lived in his flat in central Astana for more than twelve years. Last spring, the apartment above him was bought by a new owner, who immediately began extensive renovation work. According to the building's rules, such work may only be carried out between nine in the morning and six in the evening. However, my client has provided recordings which show that drilling was regularly heard late at night. He politely raised the issue on several occasions, and he was assured that the noise would stop. Unfortunately, it did not. Had the defendant respected the agreement, this matter would never have reached the court. We are therefore asking for fair compensation and a written commitment that the rules will be followed in future. Thank you, Your Honour.

Hi everyone, let me introduce myself properly. My name is Kamila Seitova, and I was born and raised in Shymkent, although I've been living in Almaty for the past three years. I come from quite a big family: I've got two older brothers and a younger sister who is, apparently, the funniest person in the whole country, or so she says. At the moment, I'm working as a junior architect, which I absolutely love. In my free time, I'm usually found in the mountains. Last summer, I hiked to Big Almaty Lake with some friends, and if I hadn't taken my camera, I would never have got into photography. Now it's my biggest hobby. As for the future, I'm hoping to study abroad for a year, perhaps in Europe, and then come back to design energy efficient buildings here in Kazakhstan. That's me in a nutshell. Nice to meet you all!

Good evening, everyone! Could I have your attention, please? For those who don't know me, I'm Ali, the groom's older brother, and I've been asked to say a few words, so please bear with me. When Arman first told me that he had met someone special at a conference in Astana, I didn't believe him. My little brother, the man who once forgot his own birthday, was in love? But then I met Aigerim, and everything made sense. She's kind, clever and, most importantly, patient enough to put up with his terrible jokes. Honestly, if they hadn't both been late for the same coffee break that day, none of us would be here tonight. So, I'd like you all to raise your glasses. To Arman and Aigerim: may your home always be full of laughter, good food and guests. To the happy couple!

So, you'll never guess what happened on our trip to Aktau last summer. My cousin Nurlan and I had been planning it for months. We'd booked a tiny guesthouse right by the Caspian Sea, and we'd promised ourselves a week of doing absolutely nothing. On the second day, we decided to drive out into the desert to see the famous rock formations. Everything was going perfectly until the car suddenly stopped in the middle of nowhere. No signal, no other cars, nothing but sand. Nurlan was convinced that we must have run out of petrol, but the tank was actually half full. Eventually, a local shepherd appeared on a motorbike, of all things, and fixed the engine in ten minutes. If he hadn't come along, we'd probably still be sitting there! Looking back, though, it was the best part of the whole holiday.

Okay, everyone, gather round the fire and find a spot on the logs. Well done, all of you. What a day! This morning we were canoeing on Lake Kolsay, and this afternoon the tents were put up in record time, even by the team who had never camped before. I'm genuinely impressed. Now, let me tell you about tomorrow. We'll be getting up at 6:30, because the hike to the upper lake is long and we want to avoid the midday heat. Breakfast will be served at 7:00, so please don't oversleep. A few rules before we start singing. Nobody leaves the camp after dark without a leader. Food must be stored in the metal boxes, not in your tents, or you might get some furry visitors tonight. And please, keep the noise down after ten o'clock. Right, who's got the guitar? Let's hear a song!

There's something about the park in autumn that always calms me down. I come here every Sunday morning, usually before the city has properly woken up. The paths have been covered in golden leaves overnight, and they crunch beautifully under my feet. Over by the fountain, an elderly couple are feeding the pigeons, just as they must have done for years. A group of teenagers are practising a dance routine near the bandstand, and a small boy is trying, without much success, to fly a kite. I've noticed that people here seem to walk more slowly than they do in the rest of Almaty. Perhaps it's the mountains in the background, already dusted with the first snow. In spring, this place is completely different: noisy, green and full of blossom. But honestly, if I had to choose, I'd pick this quiet, golden season every time.

Dear diary, it's been raining since early this morning, and I have to admit, I'm secretly delighted. My plans to go shopping in the city centre have been cancelled, so I've given myself permission to do absolutely nothing useful. I've made a huge pot of tea with milk, the way my grandmother used to, and wrapped myself in the blanket she knitted for me years ago. The rain is tapping against the window, and the streets of Astana look grey and empty. My neighbour must have forgotten his umbrella, because I've just seen him running past with a newspaper over his head. Poor man! I've been reading a novel I started last winter and never finished. If I'd known how good the ending was, I would have read it much sooner. Now the light is fading, the soup is nearly ready, and honestly, life feels pretty perfect.

Right, everyone, let's get moving! Welcome to Monday morning circuit training. I can see a few sleepy faces out there, but trust me, in ten minutes you'll be wide awake. We're starting with a gentle warm up. March on the spot, swing those arms, and breathe! Good. Now, squats. Feet shoulder width apart, chest up, and down we go. Keep your back straight; your knees shouldn't go past your toes. Excellent, Madina, that's perfect form! Next, thirty seconds of jumping jacks. Come on, push through it! I know it's tough, but if you'd skipped this class, you'd be regretting it by lunchtime. Remember, progress isn't measured by how fast you go, but by how consistently you show up. Last round now: plank position, hold it, hold it, and relax! Fantastic work, everybody. Grab some water, stretch properly, and I'll see you all on Wednesday!

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Charyn Canyon. Before we set off, I need a few minutes of your attention for a short safety briefing. Today's route is around twelve kilometres long, and it should take us roughly four hours, including breaks. The trail is mostly flat, but some sections are rocky and fairly narrow, so please watch your step. First, water. It gets extremely hot down in the canyon, so each of you should be carrying at least two litres. If you've forgotten yours, you must tell me now, not halfway through the walk. Second, please stay behind me and in front of my colleague Daniyar, who'll be walking at the back. Last year, a hiker wandered off to take photos and was eventually found by rangers three hours later. If he had stayed with the group, that could have been avoided. Any questions? Great. Let's go!

This is Mission Control. We are now twelve minutes into the flight, and all systems are performing normally. The second stage engine has been shut down as planned, and the vehicle is now coasting in a stable orbit. We were informed earlier that the fairing had been released successfully. The satellite, which was designed and built by engineers in Almaty, is now being prepared for separation. Telemetry is being received clearly from our ground station near Baikonur. If separation had been scheduled any earlier, the satellite would have been out of contact with our antennas. Separation is confirmed at 10:42. The satellite is drifting away from the upper stage, exactly as expected. Its solar panels were programmed to open two minutes after separation. Power readings are rising steadily, so the panels must have opened already. Although the hardest part is over, we will continue monitoring very closely. Congratulations, team. Excellent work today.

Welcome to the tongue twister challenge! Warm up your lips, because these lines were written to trip you up. Ready? First one, nice and slow. Six slim sailors sailed south past the salty shore of the silver Caspian Sea. Now faster! Next, a tricky one with the letter p. Patient Polina packed plenty of purple plums for a picnic in the peaceful park. Good! Try this rhyme. A clever cook from Kokshetau cooked crispy cakes, but couldn't say how. Fantastic. Now a really tough one. Whether the weather is warm or wet, Aruzhan's white woolly wellies won't get wet. Did you get that? Again! Here's another. Brave Bolat bought brown bread and buttered it brightly, but the brown bread was baked too lightly. Finally, the champion's challenge. Freshly fried fish feeds five friendly fishermen on Friday. Brilliant work! If you'd practised this yesterday, you'd be a professional already. Well done!

Ladies and gentlemen, may I have your attention, please. This is the final boarding call for passengers travelling on Steppe Air Flight 427 to Aktau. Boarding is about to close at Gate 12, and any passengers who have yet to board are kindly requested to proceed there immediately. Should you fail to present yourself within the next five minutes, your luggage will be offloaded and the aircraft will depart without you. Passengers are also reminded that, for security reasons, baggage must be kept with them at all times. Any item left unattended is liable to be removed and may be destroyed by the security services without prior warning. Under no circumstances should you agree to carry items on behalf of people you do not know. If you notice a bag or parcel that appears to have been abandoned, please do not touch it; instead, report it to a member of airport staff or a police officer straight away. Your cooperation in this matter is greatly appreciated. Thank you, and we wish you a pleasant journey.

Ladies and gentlemen, good evening and welcome aboard Steppe Air Flight 615 to Aktau. Captain Nurlan Sadykov and the crew are delighted to have you with us. Before we push back, we would ask you to direct your attention to the safety demonstration, which, however familiar it may seem, is well worth a moment of your time. Should the cabin lose pressure, oxygen masks will drop from the panel above you; do secure your own mask before assisting anyone else. Your seat belt must remain fastened whenever the sign is illuminated. Not only is this a legal requirement, it is also by far the simplest way to stay safe in unexpected turbulence. Shortly after we take off, a light dinner will be served, followed by tea and coffee. Having flown this route countless times, I can promise you a spectacular view of the Caspian as we begin our descent. We expect to land at 21:40 local time. Sit back, relax, and thank you for flying with us.

Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Almaty Two station. This is a passenger announcement. The 14:25 express service to Astana, which was scheduled to depart from platform 3, will now be leaving from platform 5. We apologise for any inconvenience this may cause. Passengers travelling to Shymkent should be aware that, owing to essential engineering work near Taraz, the 15:10 service is currently delayed by approximately forty minutes. It is not yet known whether further delays will occur, but staff on the concourse will be only too happy to advise you on alternative connections. Under no circumstances should luggage be left unattended anywhere in the station; any unattended item may be removed and destroyed without warning. When boarding, please mind the gap between the train and the platform edge, and allow passengers to step off before you get on. Should you require assistance, simply speak to a member of staff wearing a green jacket. Thank you for your patience, and we wish you a pleasant journey.

Attention, please. This train terminates at Moskva. The next station is Abay. Doors are closing; please stand clear. Ladies and gentlemen, as we approach the busiest part of the line, we would kindly remind you that it is courteous to remove your backpack and hold it by your feet, thereby leaving space for those boarding at the next stop. Seats near the doors are reserved for elderly passengers, expectant mothers and anyone travelling with small children, so do offer yours if you see someone in need. What makes the journey pleasant for everyone is not the speed of the train but the consideration shown by fellow passengers. Should you notice an unattended bag or anything suspicious, please inform a member of staff immediately rather than touching it yourself. Passengers wishing to change lines are advised to alight at Alatau, where the transfer is clearly signposted. Eating and loud music are not permitted on board. We are now arriving at Abay. Please mind the gap, and thank you for travelling with us.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome aboard the route to Medeu. This is your driver speaking. Before we set off, a few words about tickets. Fares can be paid by card or by scanning the code displayed beside the door; cash, I'm afraid, is no longer accepted on this route. Passengers found travelling without a valid ticket will be asked to pay a fine, so do make sure you've tapped in. Next stop: Dostyk Avenue. Those of you heading to the skating rink should stay on until the final stop, which, traffic permitting, we should reach in about half an hour. Seats at the front are set aside for older passengers and those with limited mobility, and I'd be grateful if you could give them up without being asked. Rarely have I seen the bus as full as it is today, so please move right down inside and keep the aisle clear. Hold on tight as we climb, because the road ahead is steep and winding. Thank you, and enjoy the mountain air.

So, you're heading to the airport? No problem at all, hop in. Now, I'll be honest with you: at this time of day, Abay Avenue tends to be gridlocked, so I'd rather take the back streets through Bostandyk. It may look like a detour, but believe me, it'll save us a good twenty minutes. I've been driving in Almaty for fifteen years, and if there's one thing I've learnt, it's that the shortest route is seldom the quickest. Are you here on business or just visiting? Visiting! Well, you've chosen the perfect season. Had you come a month later, the snow would have closed half the mountain roads. If I were you, I'd make a point of trying proper beshbarmak in a family restaurant, not one of those places aimed at tourists. And do get up to Kok Tobe at sunset; the view of the city lights is simply breathtaking. Right, here we are, Terminal 2, with time to spare. Mind your bag, and have a wonderful trip!

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, this is Captain Arman Seitkali speaking from the bridge of the Caspian Pearl. On behalf of all the crew, welcome aboard our overnight crossing from Aktau to Baku. We have now left the harbour and are sailing west at a steady cruising speed. Conditions this evening are calm, although a moderate swell is forecast after midnight, so those of you prone to seasickness may wish to remain on the lower decks, where the motion is least noticeable. Life jackets are stowed beneath every bunk, and muster stations are clearly marked on each deck. Should you hear seven short blasts followed by one long blast, proceed calmly to your muster station and await instructions from the crew. Dinner is now being served in the main restaurant on Deck 4 until 21:30. Not to be missed, incidentally, is the sunset over the open sea, which can best be enjoyed from the stern. We are due to arrive at 08:00 tomorrow morning. Thank you, and have a restful night.

Good evening, and welcome to the Hotel Altyn Dala. You must be Ms Kemelbekova; we've been expecting you. I trust your journey from Astana wasn't too exhausting? Now, you've been allocated room 714, which is one of our corner rooms, so you'll have uninterrupted views of the mountains. Here's your key card. Breakfast is served on the ground floor from 07:00 until 10:30, and I'd strongly recommend trying our baursak, freshly made each morning. Should you wish to unwind, the spa and indoor pool on the lower level are open until 22:00, and guests are entitled to complimentary use of the gym around the clock. Wireless internet is available throughout the building, and the password is printed on the back of your key card. Were you to need anything at all, whether it's a late checkout, a taxi or a restaurant recommendation, simply dial zero from your room. The lifts are just around the corner on your left. Enjoy your stay, and do let us know if there's anything else we can do.

Right, everyone, gather round, if you would. Welcome to Charyn Canyon, or the Valley of Castles, as it's often called. Take a moment to look around you. What you're seeing is the result of roughly twelve million years of erosion, carved by wind, water and frost into these extraordinary towers of red sandstone. It's often compared to the Grand Canyon, though it is, admittedly, considerably smaller. Never, however, have I met a visitor who left disappointed. The trail we're about to follow runs about three kilometres down to the Charyn River, where you'll find a shaded picnic area. Before we set off, a few ground rules. Please stay on the marked path, since the rock here is surprisingly fragile and crumbles underfoot. Drink plenty of water; temperatures on the canyon floor can be several degrees higher than up here. And do keep an eye out for lizards and, if you're lucky, a golden eagle circling overhead. Right then, cameras ready? Let's head down.

Good morning, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome aboard our sightseeing tour of Astana. My name is Aigerim, and I'll be your guide for the next ninety minutes. Should you wish to get off at any stop, simply let me know, and you can rejoin a later bus at no extra cost. On your left, you'll see the Baiterek tower, arguably the most recognisable symbol of the capital. Legend has it that a magical bird laid a golden egg in the branches of the tree of life, and it is precisely this story that inspired the design. Rising from what was, only a few decades ago, open steppe, the city has been transformed almost beyond recognition. Coming up on the right is the Khan Shatyr, a vast transparent tent housing shops, restaurants and even an indoor beach. Bear in mind that winters here are notoriously harsh, which explains why so much of city life takes place under one roof. Our next stop is the Nur Astana Mosque. Enjoy the ride!

Good afternoon, shoppers, and thank you for choosing Dala Market. Just a quick reminder that our autumn sale is now in full swing, with discounts of up to half price across the entire home and kitchen department. Not only have we reduced our cookware, but every set of bed linen is also on special offer until Sunday. For those of you with a sweet tooth, head over to aisle seven, where locally produced honey from the Almaty region is available at a remarkably low price, while stocks last. Members of our loyalty scheme are entitled to an additional discount at the checkout, so do have your card or app ready. If you've yet to join, our staff at the customer service desk would be only too happy to sign you up. Please note that the store will be closing early today, at 20:00, owing to a scheduled stocktake. The automatic tills near the entrance tend to be the quickest option. Thank you for shopping with us, and have a lovely afternoon.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to Tulpar Mall. Here is an important announcement. A young boy named Daniyar, aged about six, has been separated from his parents near the food court on the third floor. He is wearing a blue jacket and red trainers. Should anyone see him, please accompany him to the information desk on the ground floor, where his family is waiting. Our lost and found service, incidentally, is located at the same desk, and items handed in today can be collected until closing. On a lighter note, tonight at 19:00 the central atrium will be hosting a live performance by a dombra ensemble from Shymkent, followed by a fashion show featuring young Kazakh designers. Seldom do we have the chance to bring such talent under one roof, so do come along. Shoppers are reminded that the cinema is on the fourth floor, while the supermarket can be found on the lower ground level. The mall will close at 22:00. Thank you for visiting.

Good afternoon, and welcome to Shanyrak Cafe! Please, take a seat wherever you like; the table by the window has the best view of the square. I'm Madina, the owner, and I'll be looking after you today. Let me talk you through the menu. What we're particularly proud of is our lagman, pulled by hand every morning by my mother, who has been making it for over forty years. If you fancy something lighter, the beetroot salad with walnuts and goat's cheese is a firm favourite with our regulars. Having travelled all over Central Asia, I've tried to bring together the best flavours of the region, so you'll also find Uzbek plov and Kyrgyz ashlyamfu. Not to be missed, though, is our dessert of the day: honey cake with sea buckthorn cream. To drink, I'd recommend our house tea with milk and a pinch of salt, served the traditional way. Do take your time deciding, and simply wave when you're ready to order. Enjoy!

Good morning, and welcome to the Densaulyk Family Clinic. This is a reception announcement. Patients with a booked appointment are kindly asked to check in at the touch screens to your right, which will issue you with a queue number. When your number appears on the display, please proceed to the room indicated. Those of you without an appointment should register at the main desk; however, please be aware that waiting times this morning are considerably longer than usual, owing to the seasonal flu vaccination programme. Under no circumstances should you enter a consulting room until you have been called. We would also remind patients that mobile phones must be switched to silent throughout the building, and that food and drink are not permitted in the waiting area. Should your appointment need to be cancelled or rescheduled, we would ask you to notify us at least one day in advance, so that the slot can be offered to another patient. Thank you for your patience and cooperation.

Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to the Abai Central Library. I'm Dana, one of the librarians here, and I'll be showing you around. Built in the nineteen sixties and extensively renovated last year, this building houses well over half a million volumes. On the ground floor, you'll find fiction in Kazakh, Russian and English, while the upper floors are devoted to reference works and academic journals. Silence is expected in the reading rooms, though group study rooms can be booked online for up to three hours at a time. Members may borrow up to ten books for three weeks; should you need longer, renewals can easily be made through your account. Overdue items, I'm afraid, incur a small daily fine. Food is strictly forbidden beyond the cafe area, as are phone calls. It is on Thursday evenings that our most popular event takes place: an English book club, which is open to all. We also run a creative writing workshop every other Saturday. Any questions? Happy reading!

Welcome to room 7, home to the centrepiece of our collection. The painting in front of you, Dawn over the Steppe, was completed by the Almaty artist Arman Seitkali after nearly three years of work. Take a moment to step back, as only from a distance can its full scale be appreciated. Stretching across almost the entire wall, the steppe appears endless, its golden grasses bending gently under an invisible wind. Notice how the light is handled. Rather than painting the sun itself, the artist chose to hint at it, allowing a pale pink glow to spill over the horizon. On the left, barely visible, a lone rider on horseback can be seen heading east. It is often suggested that this figure represents the artist's grandfather, although Seitkali himself never confirmed this. What strikes most visitors, however, is the deep silence the painting seems to convey. When you are ready, please continue to room 8, where his earlier sketches are on display. Enjoy the rest of your visit.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and welcome to tonight's premiere at the Kino Saray cinema. It is a genuine honour to host the first public screening of The Last Caravan, a film shot entirely on location in the Mangystau region. Before the lights go down, a few practical notes. Please ensure that your phones are switched off, not merely silenced, since even the faintest glow can be distracting in a darkened auditorium. Photography and recording of any kind are strictly prohibited. Should you need to leave during the screening, kindly use the illuminated aisles and exit quietly. Immediately after the credits, the director and several members of the cast will join us on stage for a short discussion, during which you'll have the opportunity to put your own questions to them. Little did they know, when filming began in a sandstorm three years ago, that they would one day be sitting before a full house. Refreshments will be served in the foyer afterwards. Enjoy the film.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and a very warm welcome to the Kerey Concert Hall. We are thrilled to see such a full house for tonight's performance, Echoes of the Steppe. The first half of the programme features traditional kuis performed on the dombra and kobyz, while the second half brings together a symphony orchestra and a youth choir from Karaganda in an entirely new work, commissioned especially for this evening. There will be a twenty minute interval, during which drinks will be served in the upper foyer. Before we begin, may I ask you to switch off your mobile phones completely. Photography, filming and audio recording are not permitted at any time during the performance. Latecomers will be admitted only at a suitable break in the music, so as not to disturb the performers. Should the house lights flash, please return to your seats, as the second half will shortly begin. And now, without further ado, please welcome to the stage our soloist, Aruzhan Bekova!

Come closer, come closer, my friend! Welcome to the Green Bazaar, the beating heart of Almaty. Have a look at these apricots; they arrived from Shymkent only this morning, and I give you my word, you won't find sweeter ones anywhere in the city. Go on, try one, it's on the house. Now, over here we've got dried fruit of every kind imaginable: figs, prunes, golden raisins and, my personal favourite, apricots dried in the sun the traditional way. What sets mine apart from the rest is that I never use any sugar or preservatives. And the almonds? Picked from my uncle's orchard near Turkistan. Were you to buy a kilo of each, I'd throw in a round loaf of fresh tandyr bread, still warm from the oven. The prices, I assure you, are more than fair; ask anyone in this row. Well? Shall I wrap them up for you? Wonderful choice! Come back next week, and I'll have the first pomegranates of the season.

Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the zoo. My name is Timur, and I've been a keeper here for nearly ten years. Before we start, just a couple of rules. Please don't feed the animals, however much they may beg; their diets are carefully planned, and the wrong food can make them seriously ill. Tapping on the glass is also strictly forbidden. Now, if you look to your left, you'll see our pair of snow leopards, Aibar and Kunsulu. Rarely seen in the wild, these magnificent cats inhabit the high Tien Shan mountains, and it is estimated that only a few hundred remain in Kazakhstan. Note how thick their tails are; they wrap them around themselves like a scarf to keep warm. Moving on, the enclosure ahead houses our saiga antelopes, a species that was brought to the brink of extinction but has since made a remarkable recovery. Feeding time for the brown bears is at 11:30, which is well worth seeing. Follow me, please!

Good evening, you're watching the Evening Bulletin, and these are tonight's headlines. Rescuers in Burabay National Park have located two hikers who had been reported missing since Tuesday. Both were found in good health, having sheltered in a forest hut during the storm, and are said to be resting with their families. In Aktau, the first flamingos of the season have been spotted on the Caspian coast, a fortnight earlier than usual. Experts believe the mild autumn may be responsible, although it is too early to draw firm conclusions. Turning to sport, Astana's junior chess team has been crowned regional champion after a tense final that went to a deciding game. Their coach described the victory as the reward for months of relentless preparation. And finally, a bakery in Taraz has produced what is thought to be the largest baursak ever made, which was then shared with hundreds of delighted residents. The weather follows shortly. From all of us here, good night.

Good evening, and here is the weather forecast for Kazakhstan. Rarely have we seen such a sharp contrast across the country at this time of year. In the south, Shymkent and Turkestan will be basking in unseasonably warm sunshine, with highs comfortably above twenty degrees. Almaty, meanwhile, can expect a mild but hazy day, the smog likely to linger over the city until a breeze from the mountains clears the air by late afternoon. It is the north, however, that deserves our attention tonight. A cold front sweeping down from Siberia is expected to reach Petropavlovsk by dawn, bringing heavy sleet and gusty winds. Astana should brace itself for a dramatic drop in temperature, possibly as much as fifteen degrees within a single day. Drivers heading out early are strongly advised to allow extra time, as roads may well turn icy. Over on the Caspian coast, Aktau will stay dry and breezy. That's all from me for now. Wrap up warm, and have a lovely evening.

Tired of the same old weekend routine? Then listen closely, because this is the invitation you have been waiting for. Introducing the Golden Steppe Food Festival, returning to Astana this Saturday and Sunday for its most ambitious year yet. Not only will you find over sixty stalls serving dishes from every corner of Kazakhstan, but you will also be able to watch master chefs reinvent family recipes live on stage. Fancy fresh baursaks straight from the pan? They're here. Craving slowly cooked beshbarmak the way your grandmother made it? Look no further. What makes this festival truly special, though, is its atmosphere: live dombra music, craft workshops for children and a lantern parade along the river at sunset. Having sold out within days last year, tickets are expected to go fast, so don't leave it until the last minute. Book online today and enjoy twenty percent off before Friday. The Golden Steppe Food Festival. Come hungry, leave happy.

Good morning, you're listening to Healthy Minds, the podcast that takes a closer look at the habits shaping our wellbeing. I'm your host, Timur Bekov, and today we are tackling a subject that most of us, if we are honest, tend to neglect: sleep. We live in a culture where staying up late and surviving on coffee is often worn as a badge of honour. Yet research increasingly suggests that cutting corners on rest may be doing us far more harm than good. It is not only our mood that suffers, but our memory, our concentration and, perhaps surprisingly, our productivity at work. Joining me in the studio is a sleep specialist from Astana, who has spent years studying why so many of us struggle to switch off at night. We will be exploring what actually happens while we sleep, whether sleeping in at the weekend really helps, and what small changes could make a big difference. So, grab a cup of tea, though perhaps not a strong coffee, and settle in. Let's get started.

And here we go, we're into the final minute of this championship final, and the tension inside the stadium is almost unbearable! Astana United lead by a single goal, but Almaty Rovers are throwing everything at them. Never have I heard a crowd this loud. Dana Akhmetova, the Rovers' captain, picks up the ball in midfield, skips past one challenge, then another! She's into the box! Surely this is it! Oh, what a save! The keeper, having been rather quiet all night, flings herself to the right and somehow tips it round the post! Unbelievable! A corner, then, and this could well be the last kick of the game. Everyone is up; even the Rovers' goalkeeper has come forward. The ball is swung in, it's headed clear, it falls to Aruzhan, she shoots! Off the bar! And there's the whistle! It's all over! Astana United are the champions, and what a finish we have witnessed tonight. Absolutely incredible scenes here. Goodnight from all of us!

Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, welcome to the Central Stadium in Almaty for tonight's cup final! What an evening lies ahead of us. On my left, the visitors, having travelled all the way from Pavlodar, are chasing their first trophy in over a decade. On my right, your very own Almaty Snow Leopards, determined to defend the title they won so memorably last spring. Before kick off, a few important announcements. Should you need assistance at any point, please speak to a steward in a yellow jacket. Emergency exits are clearly marked at the end of every row, and we kindly ask that the stairways be kept clear at all times. Flares, glass bottles and laser pointers are strictly prohibited inside the ground. Smoking is not permitted anywhere in the stadium. Now, it is time to make some noise! Let's give a warm welcome to both teams as they walk out onto the pitch. Enjoy the match, and may the best team win!

Here, at the very top of our planet, the wind cuts through everything. For thousands of years, this frozen ocean has been covered by a thick layer of sea ice, expanding in winter and shrinking only slightly in summer. Today, however, that balance is being lost. Scientists estimate that the summer ice now covers far less of the ocean than it did a few decades ago. What is happening here does not stay here. As bright white ice gives way to dark open water, less sunlight is reflected back into space, and the ocean absorbs ever more heat. This, in turn, speeds up the melting even further. Polar bears, forced to swim greater distances in search of food, are perhaps the most visible victims. Yet the effects reach far beyond the Arctic, disrupting weather patterns that distant farmers depend upon. Were the ice to disappear entirely in summer, the consequences would be felt by all of us. The question is no longer whether the Arctic is changing, but how quickly we are prepared to respond.

Hello and welcome back to Steppe Kitchen! Today we're tackling a dish that, frankly, is often misunderstood: proper homemade manti. What most people get wrong is the dough, so let's start there. Flour, a pinch of salt and lukewarm water, kneaded until it's smooth and elastic. Once it has rested for half an hour, it'll be far easier to roll. Now, for the filling. Finely chopped lamb, plenty of onion and, crucially, a little pumpkin, which keeps everything wonderfully juicy. Season generously with black pepper and cumin. Here comes the fun part. Roll the dough thinly, cut it into squares, spoon in the filling and pinch the corners together like this. Don't worry if yours look a little rustic; nobody has ever complained about an ugly dumpling. Brush the steamer with oil, arrange the manti so they're not touching, and steam them for about forty minutes. Served with sour cream and a sprinkle of fresh dill, they're absolutely irresistible. Enjoy, and see you next week!

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for coming at such short notice. I'm Dana Sarsenova, spokesperson for the Aktau City Administration. I'm pleased to announce that, following eighteen months of consultation, construction of the new seafront promenade will begin in early spring. The project, which is being funded jointly by the city and regional partners, is expected to create several hundred local jobs. Not only will the promenade provide safer access to the Caspian shore, but it will also include cycling lanes, shaded seating and a small open air theatre. I'll take a question now. Yes, the gentleman at the front. You're asking whether the work will disrupt the summer season. That's a fair concern, and one we have taken very seriously. It has been agreed that the busiest stretches of beach will remain open throughout, with heavy work scheduled mainly for the quieter months. Further details will be published on the city website later today. Thank you all very much.

This is an emergency weather broadcast for the Almaty region. A severe storm warning has been issued and will remain in force until 6:00 tomorrow morning. Wind gusts of up to ninety kilometres an hour are forecast, accompanied by torrential rain and a risk of hail in the foothills. Residents are strongly urged to stay indoors unless travel is absolutely essential. Should you have to go out, avoid parking beneath trees and keep well away from fallen power lines. Garden furniture and other loose objects ought to be brought inside or secured without delay. Those living near mountain rivers should be prepared for rapidly rising water levels and follow any instructions given by the emergency services. Under no circumstances should anyone attempt to drive through flooded roads. Keep your phone charged, a torch within reach and an eye on official updates. Further bulletins will be broadcast every hour on this frequency. Please stay safe, look out for your neighbours, and thank you for listening.

Good morning, everyone, this is Mrs Abenova speaking with today's announcements. First, a change to the timetable: owing to a staff training session, all afternoon lessons will finish at 2:30 rather than the usual time. Buses have been rearranged accordingly, so please check the board outside the main office. Second, I'm delighted to report that our debating team, having beaten six schools in the regional final, will be representing Shymkent at the national championship in Astana next month. Congratulations to Arman, Madina and Daniyar; we're immensely proud of you. Third, a gentle reminder. Rarely has the lost property box been quite so full, and among its treasures are no fewer than eleven left trainers. If any of them happen to be yours, do come and claim them before Friday, after which they'll be donated to charity. Finally, auditions for the spring musical are being held in the assembly hall at lunchtime. Everyone is welcome, regardless of experience. Have a productive day.

Right, good morning, everyone, and welcome to today's lesson. Phones away, please, and let's get started. Today we're going to be looking at how persuasive language actually works and, more importantly, how you can use it yourselves. Here's the plan. We'll begin by analysing two short speeches, one of which is genuinely convincing and one of which, frankly, falls flat. Your first task, working in pairs, will be to figure out exactly why. Is it the structure? The choice of words? The rhythm? After that, each pair will draft a two minute pitch arguing that our school should introduce a four day week. Ambitious, I know. What I'm looking for isn't perfection, but clear arguments supported by solid evidence. Now, I appreciate that some of you find speaking in public rather daunting. Believe me, so did I at your age. But it is precisely by practising in a safe space like this that confidence is built. So, take a deep breath, and let's dive in.

Thank you for inviting me today. My name is Aigerim Tulegenova, and I'm delighted to have the opportunity to tell you a little about myself. Having graduated in environmental engineering from a university in Almaty, I spent four years working for a regional water company, where I was responsible for monitoring supply networks across several districts. What I found most rewarding was not the technical side alone, but the chance to work closely with local communities and explain complex issues in plain language. Last year, I led a small team that managed to cut water losses in one district by almost a third, which I'm genuinely proud of. That said, I'm now keen to take on a broader role, and it's precisely for that reason that your company appeals to me. Your commitment to sustainable infrastructure aligns closely with my own values. I would welcome the chance to contribute my experience while continuing to learn. Thank you, and I'm happy to answer any questions.

Good morning, Nurlan, and welcome aboard! We're really glad to have you with us. Let me give you a quick overview before you settle in. You'll be joining the product design team, which, as you'll soon discover, is a lively bunch. Sitting by the window are Aruzhan and Timur, who between them handle most of our client projects. Aruzhan, incidentally, will be your buddy for the first month, so don't hesitate to ask her anything at all. As for your tasks, this week is mainly about getting your bearings. You'll be shadowing a few meetings, reading through our style guide and, by Friday, sketching some initial ideas for the Burabay resort website. No pressure whatsoever; nobody expects miracles on day one. The kitchen is just round the corner, and the coffee machine, temperamental though it may be, is free. Lunch tends to be around one, and today it's on the company. Right, that's enough from me. Make yourself at home.

Good morning, everyone, and thank you for meeting us. My name is Madina, and I am the founder of LinguaSteppe, an app designed to help teenagers across Kazakhstan learn English through short daily games. Millions of pupils in small towns have little or no access to qualified English teachers, and private tutoring is out of reach for most families. What we have built is a solution that works on even the cheapest smartphone, adapts to each learner's level and requires no constant internet connection. Since launching our pilot in Shymkent six months ago, we have seen remarkable results. Not only are our users practising for longer, but their test scores have risen noticeably compared with those of their classmates. Schools are now approaching us, rather than the other way round. We are seeking investment to expand into three more regions. We are not asking you to take a leap of faith, but to back an idea that is already working. Thank you, and I am happy to take your questions.

Hi Dana, it's Madina. Sorry to ring so early, but I wanted to catch you before your meeting. I've just come off the phone with the venue in Astana, and I'm afraid there's been a bit of a mix up with the booking. Apparently, the conference hall we reserved has been double booked, which, as you can imagine, came as quite a shock. The good news is that they've offered us a larger room on the second floor at no extra cost. Admittedly, it lacks the view over the river, but it does have far better sound equipment, so I'm inclined to accept. Were we to say no, we'd have to start looking all over again, and with only three weeks to go, that strikes me as rather risky. Could you have a think and let me know by lunchtime? Also, the printed programmes need updating, so let's not send them off just yet. Anyway, call me back when you can. Speak soon, bye!

Distinguished guests, colleagues and friends, it is an honour to welcome you to this year's conference on the future of education. Over the past decade, technology has transformed not only the way we learn, but also what we consider worth learning. Today, students are expected to think critically, collaborate across cultures and adapt to challenges that did not exist a few years ago. Our speakers will explore how artificial intelligence, personalised learning and language skills can open doors for young people everywhere. I encourage you to ask difficult questions, challenge assumptions and leave this event with ideas you can put into practice tomorrow.

Good afternoon, distinguished guests, faculty members, proud families and, of course, my fellow graduates. It is a privilege I never imagined I would have, standing here on behalf of this graduating class. Four years ago, most of us arrived in Astana barely knowing where the library was, let alone what we wanted from life. What we found here was not merely a set of lectures but a community that challenged us at every turn. Rarely have I met people so willing to stay up until dawn helping a friend with an essay that was not even their own. Having struggled through endless exams, we have learnt that failure is seldom final and that persistence tends to pay off in the long run. It is our teachers, above all, who deserve the credit for that lesson. As we leave, the world may seem uncertain, yet I would argue that uncertainty is precisely where opportunity lies. So let us go out there and make our country proud. Congratulations, everyone, and thank you!
